reviews.title: Like stiff tissue paper!!!
reviews.text: I bought this because I had trouble getting the Scott's Rapid-Dissolve RV t.p. (the brand I've been buying for a few years now).  There is absolutely no comparison between the Scott's and this stuff!  The Scott's brand is the closest to "regular" toilet paper, and yet it does dissolve with no problem.  The Luxsoft does dissolve well, but that is just about its ONLY virtue.  It IS two-ply, but VERY THIN, so the tendency is to use more.  It definitely does not FEEL like "normal" toilet paper, whereas I would be OK with using the Scott's at home (and have done so).  As another reviewer pointed out, the perforations in the two layers of the roll do not line up - first time I have EVER run across that in toilet paper!  I bought this in a hurry, and did not take time to read the reviews then - ONLY noticed the average rating of 4.4.  I can't understand how ANYONE could rate this stuff a "5" - unless their only criterion is quick dissolving  ... and at least it does do that.

reviews.text:
This isn't your super plush home use toilet paper of course. It isn't embossed or quilted. It's just a flat 2-ply tissue made for large roll dispensers.

It's absorbent and stands up to a little dampening, but does fall apart when thoroughly wet, so it is less likely to cause clogs or problems in septic systems. It's not super soft, but it's not scratchy.

Good commercial quality tissue.

reviews.title: Long lasting toilet paper
reviews.text: Our family owned restaurant is always looking for better quality/more cost efficient products. This toilet paper is similar to the smaller rolls of Scott 1000 sheets. It's a thin, large roll. It's not the softest, but it lasts quite a while, and is great for commercial use.

I've used Scott brand toilet paper for years now and have yet to be disappointed.
This isn't the thick, plush, wiping with a cloud toilet paper that you'll find with other brands. It's relatively thin but absorbent and does the job well. Huge plus: you won't be clogging your toilet with huge wads of fluffy tp! It's completely safe for your septic system.
Also, if you're like me and use the bathroom quite frequently then you know that it's not unusual to go through nearly a whole roll of tp each day. I have never had that problem with Scott brand. One regular sized roll lasts me anywhere from 3-7 days.
This particular roll (JUMBO size) seems to be somewhat thicker than the small rolls you buy at the grocery store. I think it has to be considering how heavy the jumbo roll is.
You typically find these in public restrooms but I'm using them at home. They're just barely too large for my toilet paper holder but after using it for a couple of days it gets down to the perfect size and I love that I'm not replacing it with a new roll every other day.
I highly recommend this product!

reviews.title: Great combo, easy on sore or not sore noses
reviews.text:
Of course, the Kleenex brand has become synonymous with facial tissue. So usually, there is no question about quality, only about which kind of Kleenex, or what box design you want. By the way, the box design on the packages I received are a pleasant, generic green design that would be okay in nearly any room.

Now, I've tried the lotion versions, but did not like them. The lotion was just too much moisture and it made my nose break out on both sides of the nostrils. So, I was a bit skeptical of these, but hoped coconut oil and aloe would be better.

I am happy to say I've been using these daily, and have had no adverse reactions. I haven't broken out, and the tissues feel pretty nice. I could see these being a 'go-to' in the event of a bad cold or allergy attack.

The tissues are so soft to the touch. They also feel thicker than average, but that could be solely because of the oils in them. By the way, I love that coconut oil and aloe are in these tissues.

Over all, I am very happy with these. I can see definitely keeping these on hand for colds or flu, and definitely for the winter, when skin often gets so dry from the cold air. Very good product.

reviews.title: We’ve Used Thousands of Various Wipes. Thoughts About These. Ingredients Noted.
reviews.text:
We have multiple children, including those still in diapers. No bidet use for them, at this time. So, we have literally used thousands and thousands of wipes, bought by the cases, over the last several years; and, from near a dozen brands. From the bargain basement finds to the premium priced will give them a try version. Flushable, and non-flushable. Scented and unscented. We are looking for the holy grail of wipes. These are competitive, but are not going to be our top choice. [Right now our top choice is the non-flushable version, for our children, but when traveling, flushable is needed, so a try we gave these.]

What did we receive? A soft plastic type rectangular package (classic packaging for wipes) measuring about 8” x 4½” x 2”. Is this package resealable? Yes. Is it durable? Yes, with careful use. How many wipes are within each package? (60). What size is each wipe? About 6” x 8”. Are these scented? No. Are these effective? Yes. Do they stay intact? Yes, when carefully used. Can these be used on children or adults? Yes, that’s why we selected these. Can we use these for when we travel? Yes, that’s why we selected these? How is the price? They are at a premium? Summary: These work, as they should. Can you give these as a gift? Awkward, however, not so if for a baby shower (however, there are wipes specifically targeted for babies, these are not noted to be marketed for babies). Are these wipes premoistened. Yes, amply. Can these wipes be flushed? The packaging recites “Flushable Wipes.” Will these wipes disintegrate? The package reads: “Easily Disintegrates.” Are these gentle on the skin? Using my face, I found they were? Would I replace my current baby wipes for these? No. What percentage is water? The listing noted the wipes are 99% water, are they gentle on sensitive skin? Yes, adult tested, on sensitive are of face. Are these made without alcohol? The packaging indicated no alcohol. What are these made from? The listing, not the packaging, indicated 100% plant-based material.

Perfect for on the go and fit perfectly in travel / diaper bags

What are the ingredients
(1) Purified water.
(2) Cetylpyridinium Chloride. What is that? It is a quaternary ammonium salt. What’s that for? Typically for disinfectants, surfactants, fabric softeners, and as antistatic agents.
(3) Sodium benzoate. What is that used for? It is a preservative commonly used in foods, pharmaceuticals, and cosmetics.
(4) Lodopropynyl butylcarbamate. What is that used for? Typically, as a preservative used in cosmetics, wet wipes (toilet paper), and other personal care products
(5) Glycerin. What is that for? Typically for retaining moisture
(6) Aloe barbadensis leaf extract. What is that? Aloe vera juice. Since this notes this aloe vera product contains whole leaf extract, it does not note whether that extract has been decolorized.
(7) Tocopherol. What is that? It a class of naturally occurring chemical compounds related to Vitamin E.

The reader is encouraged to independently do their own research surrounding the ingredients.

Where were these made? China.

Weight of the wipe package was near (14) ounces.

Are there warnings? Yes. What? The listing notes them on the package, but, for instance, not more than one (1) of these can be flushed at a time and local restrictions may restrict their use. I also thought information lacking about the exact composition of the wipes was missing.
Based on the totality, which includes that premium price, and noting the quantity of (60), these are not what I consider the bargain priced perfect wipes, but they are competitive, so four (4) stars, at most.

I hope my thoughts were of assistance.

reviews.text: This is really soft toilet paper and good for the environment.  I enjoy using it.  There seems to be a subtle, pleasant fragrance.  But I actually thought this was single ply until one of my sheets split into two plys.  Indeed, I think this is less substantial than the single ply at my doctor's office when I visited this afternoon.  So the rolls are less substantial than I'm used to and so not as great of a deal as I'd hoped.  I need extra to feel like I'm getting coverage, and 300 sheets already isn't that thick of a roll in this era of beefed up rolls (to save packaging.  It's in the ballpark with pricing, but I'll stick with my 100% recycled t.p. For the foreseeable future.  I somewhat prefer the feel of this one, but I want more substance and amount on a roll, all the more when you're mail ordering and so using up a large box.  Sorry to say that.  It's good to get renewable bamboo t.p. on the market.  I'll see if they make some changes in the future.

reviews.title: Not Worth It
reviews.text:
Living in the desert, and having a high-traffic carpet – my feet tend to get dirty a lot.

And, I don’t relish going to bed with dirty feet (who would). I also don’t have the “flexibility” to scrub them over a tub, and putting them in a sink? Not too easy either.

I have used baby wipes (like another reviewer) and gotten some success. And, there are “big” body wipes (for when you’re camping) that work quite well.

Arm & Hammer Baking Soda has been the “go-to” for almost everything:

🔋 Baking Soda + Water = used to clean battery cables
🛁 Baking Soda + White Vinegar = good for drains & clogs
🧺 Baking Soda + Washing Detergent = very clean laundry

You get the idea.

What it doesn’t mix well? Personal care! These wipes smell nasty. And, if you have foot odor (thankful I don’t) – it’s a toss-up between natural ugly smell or the ugly smell of the wipes.

They clean as average as baby wipes or other personal care wipes. To even clean “moderate” dirt I need two (2) per foot). The smell is atrocious.

This is one product that Arm & Hammer could do without.

reviews.title: functional, but not soft enough, and TOO SMALL.
reviews.text:
In these desperate times of pandemic-caused empty store shelves, I've been forced to start ordering many of my paper products online. I reluctantly selected this item, because at the time it was one of the few cases of facial tissues Amazon had available that had a reasonably acceptable delivery date. I suspected they probably weren't going to be quite as good as the store brand I normally buy at one of the nation's major grocery chains. Turns out, I was right.
Aside from the annoyance that there are only 100 tissues per box (the ones I normally buy contain 210), I also, after trying them, noticed that they are not as soft as the ones I usually get. Not that they're sandpaperesque, don't get me wrong. But I'd hate to see how sore my nose would get if I were to use these all day with a cold and a runny nose.
Thirdly, they are too small. Standard tissues are 12 x 22.5cm. These are just 10.5 x 21cm. While not a huge difference in size, it still takes some getting used to. I'd have preferred if they'd made them standard size and charged a bit more.
Ultimately, I don't hate them enough to throw them out. My family and I will use up the ones we have. But when/if it comes time to order more tissues online, I intend to go with another brand.

reviews.title: Shouldn’t be so difficult!
reviews.text:
Why did toilet paper become so complicated?
It took me, a picky person committed to finding best value that meets my needs, several “tries” and tons of comparison metrics between products on Amazon to find what I wanted and ensure I’m NOT being “ripped off” on price.

Then what happened? They withdrew that product from sale. Ugh. They have so many package options (#rolls) and new sizes (sq inches on rolls) and designations/equivalents of rolls (mega, family, family-mega, regular, etc) that it involves a significant investment of time to choose your toilet paper. It’s ridiculous. It gives the false impression, in my opinion, that the consumer has infinite “choices” while in actuality, it has the effect of a shell game. Come on, manufacturers. It’s toilet paper. You are earning a bad rep.

This one was great. Met all my needs. But is withdrawn from Subscribe and Save. :(

reviews.text:
Coin Tissue 300pcs Compressed Coin Toilet Paper Tablets Flushable Wipes for Sensitive Skin is a small sanitation system that you could carry.

The whole thing consists of 300 compressed tissues and a small six tissue holder. The idea is that you put six (6) compressed tissues in the holder in one of the two compartments. When you need a tissue, you remove it from compartment one (the dry one) and put it in compartment two (the wet one). Add some water and the tissue expands to normal size.

When you compare 300 compressed 2-ply tissues to a box of 2-ply tissues, the volume is much less.

reviews.title: Total Genius!
reviews.text: Absolutely brilliant! These tiny "pellets," for lack of a better word, are stacked into one side of the little holder and the other side is filled with water. Then you just put the whole thing into your purse, backpack, car, etc. When you need a wet wipe, simple place a paper pellet into the lid and pour a bit of water on it. Voilà! It instantly turns into a full sized wet wipe right in front of your eyes! Coolest thing ever!! There are tons of paper pellets included and you can just put a bunch in a zip lock baggie if you wish instead of using the little device. Any source of water will work. The wipes are soft, thick and kind of stretchy. Perfect for face, hands ...or anywhere. I am keeping some in my car and the majority in my  emergency supply kit. So tiny. So clever. So worthwhile. Highly recommend!

reviews.title: Didn't work for me - but maybe it will for you!
reviews.text:
I love the idea of this product! I have recently switched to a bidet and found myself reevaluating my relationship with toilet paper. Sadly, there is no electrical outlet anywhere near the toilet so I was not able to get a fancier model with a dryer on it. I still need the TP, but strictly in a blotting function. As my anatomy requires a spray and a blot both 'fore and aft, I am still using more TP than I would like.

This product showed up in my "recommends", and I thought what a great idea! Here are the positives:

1. This is high quality flannel. Survived a wash and a dry like a champ. Very soft on sensitive skin.
2. Why not add a little whimsy to your bodily functions? The prints are fun.
3. I like the inclusion of the cardboard roll, and instructions for completely replacing your toilet roll on the spindle. We've all learned reflexively to reach for that TP holder, and this makes it easy.

What didn't work for me...

1. I am more of a TP wadder. The flannel, being soft, does not so much wad in the hand as just... hang there. That meant that more of my bare hand made contact with the area in question when blotting. Of course I wash my hands afterward, but it was still... disconcerting.
2. Some parts of my business retained more water, which brought the absorbency of the flannel to light - specifically, that it is not especially absorbent. The "aft" portion retained less water to begin with, so these flannels actually worked a bit better for that purpose.

IF you are someone who may have smaller hands, or less leftover bidet water clinging to your anatomy, this might work for you. I think specifically, these would be great for kids, whether using a bidet or not, just because they might be able to get more hand coverage. If you're not sure whether they'll work for you, I would try and cut a piece of fabric (flannel if you have it, but also a thick t-shirt material would work for demonstration purposes) to the size of these wipes, and check out the ergonomics for yourself before committing. I will likely sew two to four of these together to make a larger surface area and see how that works, and if it doesn't, will be transitioning to standard sized cotton washcloths, because I'd rather not be flushing paper down the toilet multiple times a day.

reviews.title: We love Charmin!
reviews.text:
We love Charmin around our home. It's what we buy on a regular basis, and have for many years now. It's so wonderfully soft and it doesn't irritate me, like some toilet paper.

This particular packaging has "Super Mega Rolls", meaning each roll is the equivalent of 6 regular rolls. As you can imagine, the rolls are very large. (We normally buy the "Mega Rolls", just because those usually have a better price where we shop. ) If you have smaller children that like to dunk whole rolls of toilet paper into the toilet or generally ruin whole rolls at a time, I'd recommend smaller rolls, because they're basically wiping out 6 rolls at a time with these rolls. My children are *mostly* out of this phase(although since I wrote that I'm sure I'll find a ruined roll), so I love not having to change the toilet paper roll as often with these. (That sounds lazy, but with 3 little guys to take care of, all those little chores add up to a full day. Every convenience counts!)

Overall, Charmin is wonderful toilet paper, and simply the best, in my little old opinion. If you like the convenience of not having to change the toilet paper roll as often, "Super Mega Rolls" might be just the thing for you.

reviews.title: Great concept, multiple uses and totally flushable..!!
reviews.text:
Wowza!! Wet wipes for grown-ups… What a novel concept! x2 the size of baby wipes and x2 the thickness- not bad qualities to have for their intended purpose!

Cool mint feels soft and refreshing to skin and for those who do not know, there’s a natural analgesic property in mint… So, it’s a little extra perk when using! *note: there is no residual cooling tingle feeling from the mint (no icy hot left on your muffins!) So, these can be used without concern of being too strong in their effect.. rather the mint property is just refreshing! Oh, and no worries your tush is dry a moment after use- I’m pretty sure these wipes have magical powers?!

I see these being exceptionally beneficial for anyone post partum- bc, let’s face it ladies, even the softest toilet paper can be rough after giving birth!! These I’m sure would be a welcomed treat when one had upset stomach or illness that caused diarrhea… for us, we had unique circumstances- as currently a little one on the autistic spectrum is staying in our home from the local shelter… He has among other things; sensory issues and fears using restroom. One of his angsts is cleanliness when using the bathroom- we were using half a roll of toilet paper each time we had to go potty and clogging toilets without fail.. not fun!!

Surprisingly, getting these has saved me and my very overworked plunger a lot of headache! I was worried we would struggle to flush wipes but, all has worked as expected thus far… best part of all, we alleviated the stressors when using the bathroom- this is huge!! **most likely x1 wipe will suffice and do the job intended, fine. Fear not, if x2-3 are used.. these will still flush without incident.

Sold in a set of 6 individual packs. These would be so handy when camping or boating.. any foreign travel- Ha! I’d pack these along for sure! One could even leave a pack in the car for emergencies.. The individual packs are small and provide easy access with a flap door- i’ve got nothing but praise for the product! Sold at a price point of $20 for 6- it’s a bit more pricey then baby wipes. But, The ability to flush along with the ease and convenience of use makes it a worthy purchase. Sorry for any over share above- but, hoping the info can help your decision- stay safe.. and clean ha ha!!

reviews.title: Strong, but not as soft as other tissues
reviews.text: I’m all for products that help the environment. I’ve been using bamboo toilet paper, so I more or less knew what to expect with these tissues. They are soft, but not as soft as a fluffy Kleenex or Puffs tissue. But, they are definitely stronger. These tissues are three-ply, crimped at the ends to hold them together, and stand up to a lot. You will get more use out of one of these tissues than you will Kleenex or Puffs, so if you have a cold and a very runny nose, you’ll likely go through fewer of these. The downside is your nose will probably get irritated from continued use of these being that they are a little rougher and don’t have the lotion feel of some tissues to protect your nose when you’re repeatedly reaching for another tissue. As with many products, there’s a trade-off, and you’ll have to decide what’s most important to you.

reviews.title: The UE Megablast has replaced our Echo....sound is infinitely better !
reviews.text:
UPDATE: It is not well integrated with ALEXA at all...many times, it will be "stuck" in a loop and repeat things until I do a hard reset. Sound quality is top notch but I have grown increasingly frustrated with it.

I have previously owned the UE Boom and am a big fan of their bluetooth speakers. When I heard about the UE Megablast, I wanted to get my hands on it. It is MUCH bigger than the Blast (see pic below next to the large jar of peanut butter) and so is the sound. It really fills the entire room! Caveat: If you listen to a lot of classical music or jazz, you may find the UE boom slightly too "bass-y". I occasionally enjoy classical music but mainly listen to country, pop, and R&B. It features a 360* speaker although I would estimate more like 300* as the black band is pretty wide. Not a big deal at all but worth noting. I also LOVE the integrated Alexa feature. In fact, the UE has delegated the Echo that was in our kitchen (central location) to the bedroom. Once you listen to music on the Megablast, the Echo sounds flat! It is also waterproof although I have no plans of taking it for a swim. It's too bulky in my opinion to be really portable. Perfect for keeping poolside but not suitable as a hand held boom box. My UE speakers also came with the optional dock and I highly recommend buying it. Much simpler to simply place on the dock for charging vs fiddling with the USB cable. The software is great - I had no trouble syncing it with my iPhone. Finally, and this is a minor suggestion/criticism - I wish that it had a band of lights around the top or bottom that lit up when using Alexa - similar to Echo. The only part that lights up is a tiny band on top of the speakers which is hard to see from across the room. Again, very minor quibble thus no deduction

reviews.text:

I like the visual design of this guy, but thats where it stops.

For me, the sound is not so good. Kind of tin-can-y and no bass at all.

Also, I DONT like that it has a mic and acts as a speakerphone. It tends to make and break BT connections during calls, stealing away the audio from my phone.

Last, the way it operates, turns on, times out, turns off, is kind of annoying. To turn on you hold a button for 2 seconds - annoying. To turn off, hold for 10 seconds, wow! If the paired phone leaves the area, the speaker will beep intermittently until it comes back or you get up and turn it off - annoying. Does not pair automatically when turned on, you have to manually connect from your phone every time... Its the little things, and for me, this speaker is a pain!

reviews.title: Excellent BT-speaker for the price.
reviews.text:
I am loving this thing. The battery seems to last forever. I charge it overnight and turn it on in the morning to listen to music while I'm up and about around the house, then I work in the evenings (2nd shift) and take it with me, listening to music on the road. The at work. Then on the way home. It says it's rated for up to 12hrs battery life but I'm suspicious that it might actually be more. Although I haven't counted, and it's not on *all* the time (the first couple of hours I'm at work I'm with co-workers, it's only later that I'm alone and I crank it up). Also if I'm in the bedroom I usually have it on the charger while in use, and at work if my phone has a full charge it's plugged into my computer. Either way I've never had the battery die on me.

I used the NFC to connect it to my Samsung Galaxy S3 with zero issues, found it immediately, and reconnects without fail every time.

Sound quality is very good for this price range ($29.99 w/Prime at the time I bought it), though I generally keep the volume maxed and just use my phone volume to control it (another reason I'm surprised the battery lasts so long). I'm not expect high fidelity so I'm not really judging it on that, it's better than some of those tinny, small speakers, it beats most generic beige "PC speakers" you'd usually find at work. It doesn't hit super highs or deep lows, but it does the job for something that's portable and BT-based.

Range is what you'd expect from BlueTooth, about 10ft w/no obstructions. Walk around a corner and it'll start stuttering. Same as every BT speaker or headset I've ever had.

So for the price and expectations I'll give it 5-stars. Of course you could do better but the price would start to jump pretty quick.

reviews.title: Here's the most thorough review you'll find of this speaker:
reviews.text:
For most people, a $30 speaker doesn't require much review. Either it works well or it doesn't, and most reviews will stop there. Since I ordered this speaker in hopes of putting it next to the bed in my motorhome and using it with a Chromecast, I tested it in a level of depth normally reserved for much more expensive audio equipment before committing it to the task.

First, the non-sound quality aspects of it: The construction is actually really great. Yes, the plastic feels cheap, but each individual part is injection-molded with no visible seams or flashing and it is assembled with very consistent and high tolerances. It looks fantastic and the "flame" light creates a lovely ambiance in a dark room, although you'll never mistake it for an actual flame. The buttons are positioned so that they are easy to reach and use while not breaking up the classy looks. There is also a decorative ring around the gap for the speaker that will keep most debris and all but the smallest of fingers from getting in there to damage the driver. When playing bass-heavy music, it looks like a teeny subwoofer, comically extruding up and down in there while still keeping the classy looks. Lastly, there is a thoughtfully-included 1/4-20 female thread in the bottom for mounting it on tripods, light stands, or other standard photography/lighting equipment. It's a very nice balance of fabulous aesthetics, practical design, and quality construction.

I have a standard suite of songs and content that I use to test products like this, but I usually only skim through them or don't bother when I'm not expecting much (such as when testing a $30 Bluetooth speaker). As I previously said, I plan to use it to watch TV and movies in my RV and I am very discerning, so I wanted to know if it was up to the job and spent a lot of time piping FLAC/Tidal into it and evaluating how my test gamut of content sounded.

The "bassiest" songs I use are World Famous by Zero Zero, Turn Down for What by who gives a damn, and More Human than Human by White Zombie. As expected, this poor little speaker fell completely flat on bass reproduction. Not much can be expected from a driver that's only a little bit bigger than a quarter, after all. Upper harmonics of the bass notes did come through, especially on acoustic and electric bass vs. synth, but that only served to showcase how badly it lacked in low end. Still, those upper harmonics were better than the sub-100Hz notes being completely absent. I didn't bother with the F16 flyover test, and the thundercracks at the beginning of Garth Brooks' The Thunder Rolls sounded more like distant thunder than lousy weather outside of my window. I give it credit for reasonably accurately reproducing that much. The KILLER slides in More Human Than Human came through better than a $30 set of earbuds might, but they still sounded flat and diminished.

Alannah Myles' Black Velvet became decidedly soft, and not in a good way. The breathy whispers in the intro of the song won't even come through on most cheap speakers. This speaker did make them audible, but not understandable and I had to listen very closely for them. The acoustic guitars sounded ok, if not a little diminished. The bass guitars were completely flat. The percussion was delivered well, but not well enough. It sounded good, but not real.

Moving on the Unbelievable by EMF, one of my favorite test songs, I was heartbroken. It's a very complicated song with acoustics, electrics, percussion, piano, and synth all going at once. The song is very difficult to reproduce accurately without everything smearing together. The percussion was, like in Black Velvet, just ok. At least the cowbell and tambourine were distinguishable. The synth and electric bass ran together and were hard to tell apart, while the lead electric that accompanies the piano stood out with the now-familiar "good but not real" sound quality.

While not musically distinctive in any special way, Epic by Faith No More is a fun and energetic song that was very poorly mastered when it was new in the early 90s and hasn't been remastered since (that I know of). The poor mastering makes it a good inclusion for testing because good speakers combined with a little EQ can really bring it around and make the song punch. Sadly, the song was a complete waste on this speaker, and that's all I can say about it.

The most important test for me was dialogue in podcasts, youtube, movies, TV, etc. Here, it failed spectacularly. Although I have naturally lost the upper frequencies with age (I'm in my mid-40s) I still have exceptional hearing. Despite this, at 24 inches the dialogue was barely clear enough to understand what was going on, and at 3 feet I might as well have been listening to a conversation in the next room. I could hear talking, but not understand what was being said. This was at full volume! There is a loud air conditioner directly over the bed in my camper, and dialogue from this speaker will NEVER overcome that level of ambient noise. I'll have to look elsewhere for a speaker for my camper. The other TV is piped into the truck speakers, so I won't even be able to use it up front.

I gave this speaker 3 stars because the looks, design, and construction quality are amazing. It will fit in almost anywhere, look nice, and the light can create a nice ambiance. As a speaker, it tries but fails. If you want it for mood lighting and soft Miles Davis or Frank Sinatra playing on the table during a date, it will do that. If the sound will be a primary focus, look elsewhere.

I have the left speaker in a corner next to woofer and the right speaker (with all the controls on my desk (7.5 feet away) which is convenient.
I do not understand why these speakers (as with others) do not include a balance control since I suspect there are others that do not sit in middle of sound. I had fixed this with an older setup using a volume control to turn down the close speaker so am using same control again but it would be nice to have on right speaker.
I do like the remote. Just need to put some red finger nail polish on bottom to identify whats up. Like sound and solid construction.

reviews.title: Incredible sound, fair price.
reviews.text:
This product has officially impressed me. I'm glad I went ahead with the purchase, apprehensive though I may have been, as 250.00 dollars isn't chump change for me. I'm upgrading from a god-knows-how-old Klipsch THX 2.1 setup, which has been tried and true, but left me wanting more after all of these years. The highs and mids reveal things to me that I simply had not heard with my old speakers. Crisp, clear and sound true to the real crash of the cymbal and crunch of the guitar... The lows are punchy and tight, powerful, but adjustable and not overbearing (I'm an avid metal listener, and don't often require ridiculous bass). Overall, I have to say the sound is incredible considering I spent what I did. Also, the bluetooth aptX functionality is amazing (provides near-lossless sound over BT), and I appreciate that level of detail.

The only constructive criticism I have regarding the setup as a whole, is the remote. It really is terrible haha. A little hockey puck that is easy to fumble around, and you have to be sure you have it properly oriented every time as it's an IR remote (as opposed to BT or WiFi), meaning you have to have it pointed right at the device for it to work. This can be an annoyance if you are in a darkly lit room.

Still, the product overall is worthy of 5 stars in my opinion. Well done!

reviews.title: Perfect speaker for the garage gym - haven't tested the waterproof feature
reviews.text:
This speaker meets the needs for the garage gym at work and so far has really good sound and play time on it. I do turn off the flashing lights in an attempt to ensure I can get more music time out of it, and every now and then I will hit the color lights button to jazz things up a bit.
The speaker comes with a small piece of rope to put through a loop to use as a carrying handle (I didn't attach it). It has a 3.5 mm x 3.5 mm plug (both 'male' ends) to plug in an external source. The power cable is a USB to USB-C charging cable, and there is no 110 outlet plug associated with it, so ya know.
It was super easy set up, easy to connect (showed up as M8 in my bluetooth device finder) and the music was going within seconds of unboxing the speaker.
When switching playing devices (cell phones for this example) I had to go into my settings and disconnect from the speaker in order for another phone to "see" the speaker and then connect.
Happy listening.

reviews.text: Love this speaker! In addition to having great sound, the LED lights flash along with the music. This thing can really pump out some sound with bass. Very easy to connect with Bluetooth. USB-C charging which is good to have too. It's also waterproof too, although I don't really use speakers around a pool much. reviews.title: Another top tier option!
reviews.text: [[VIDEOID:f198fe62ffa067db2450b8de2ae1fc0c]] I've used Eduplink speakers before and as a regular user of various portable speakers I always place them at the top in terms of sound quality, balance and delivery. This continues that trend with the only real difference being the standout baby blue color of the speaker itself which feels unique without looking gaudy or obnoxious. In other words, it improves the physical look of it without trying too hard.. One of the features it utterly masters is the multiple Bluetooth link, easily pairing with another speaker without any lag or difficulties in syncing which sets it apart from many of its competitors. Multi link is becoming more common but the pairing issue is still a hindrance on many models, a hindrence that is non existent here with the Eduplink. As usual, it has gorgeous led lights that fill the speakers, bass ends and keen outer inlays with alternating colors and patterns that suit the music well while single or paired up and the ability to charge devices off it freely thanks to a large power ank is simply icing on the cake here.. Ultimately, this is another well built, sonically pleasing and visually appealing speaker from a name that I truly believe is soon to become household.. At least among audiophiles.

reviews.title: Packs A Punch
reviews.text:
I was very surprised at how great this speaker sounds. It packs quite a punch. Crystal clear sound quality, a great amount of bass, and it can handle being loud. Obviously there is a limit to all speakers ,but I turned this up past my desired listening volume and got no speaker vibrations. I fully charged the speaker and got around 9 hours of play (6 continuous during work and 3 the following day) before it said, “battery low” and I decided to plug it up. I then let it play while plugged up: a usb-c to usb cable running from the speaker to a wall charger: and it actually charged while being used. The LED lights are fun; they change according to the music…it’s a powerful little party pill.

My only concerns/complaints are:
(1) the ends are not protected. The speakers are exposed so I will need to be careful with it while using it on a jobsite…but not a huge issue.
(2) I have not figured out if there is a way to turn off the lights…I can imagine a scenario where I will not want those lights flashing but it hasn’t happened yet.

reviews.title: Switches Between Two Paired Devices; Richer Sound, Clearer Voices From Sony Bravia TV
reviews.text:
This BOSE SOUNDLINK COLOR BLUETOOTH SPEAKER may not be the ideal portable speaker for serious audiophiles--because it has no treble/base buttons, only volume buttons--but I love mine. The sound is rich and full, whether it's paired with my old Sony Bravia TV, iPad2, or Kindle Fire, or connected by AV stereo cable (3.5mm M/M) to my MP3 player's headphone jack. The volume is controlled by the device the speaker is connected to, or by the plus/minus volume buttons on the speaker itself. The speaker also has an Aux button for the direct cable connection, and a Skip button that lets you go forward or backward in your music selections.

This Bose portable speaker can support two Bluetooth-connected devices at once, so you can switch between two devices (e.g., an iPad and a Kindle Fire) without repeating the pairing process every time. A great feature! The speaker automatically connects with the last-connected Bluetooth device, and switches devices when you press the Bluetooth button. The speaker's voice prompts help you with pairing, and tell you which two devices are currently paired. The voice prompts can be disabled, if you wish.

This Bose speaker is definitely an improvement over the speakers built into my old Sony Bravia TV. Voices are much clearer--including the dialogue from British TV shows--and the sound is far richer. Of course, using this speaker instead of a TV sound bar is only a temporary solution, because the speaker needs regular recharging. When fully charged, it delivers sound for many hours (up to 8) and outlasts the charge on the [[ASIN:B004B8GF7Y TaoTronics® Bluetooth Transmitter]] that I added to my non-Bluetooth-enabled TV.

Whether the TaoTronics transmitter was connected to the TV's headphone jack or to the TV's AV ouputs, this speaker paired instantly. However, when the TV transmitter was connected to the AV outputs, the speaker produced some static unless it was positioned close to the TV. When the TV transmitter was connected to the headphone jack, the speaker produced no static at all, no matter where it was positioned (within the Bluetooth range).

This Bose speaker charges quickly with the included AC adapter and USB cable. Pressing the speaker's power button produces a battery indicator that glows red, amber, or green to indicate the current level of charge. The speaker is lightweight enough to carry around in a backpack or tote bag. There is a case available (see [[ASIN:B00NJGRKG4 Bose SoundLink Color carry case]]), but I don't think a case is needed, because the speaker seems to be sturdily constructed.

reviews.title: A Great Pocket mp3 player with a Superb Built In Speaker
reviews.text:
At last, a good speaker sound for my SDHC MP3 collections. It does have port for earphones but I only use its speaker. The controls were hard to fathom --- I almost gave up --- but after a teeth clinched, determined 30 minutes got the hang of it. A bit unfriendly, way too simple screen readings, not detailed enough for full information control. But I got it to work and am happy I did. Right now it's just great!

My ENT ear doctor said no more ear buds or headphones. Save your what's left of your ears. So, gave up all my ear buds on mp3 players. First I used players with clumsy blue tooth or wired portable speakers, an awkward pain. I webbed for a pocket mp3 player with a speaker that works without need for earphones. Near impossible until I found Degen's great, great speaker. It's splendid for my downloaded to SDHCs my MP3 books, lectures, BBC shows, Bowery Boys History, CSPAN, NPR, MP3s, WNYC, other MP3 Downloads. Super clear sound, with a powerful speaker volume more than I need. Problem solved. I am very happy.

Its radio reception is good here in New York City. I don't even need to extend the built in antenna. Good sound too. But I have yet to figure out how to change from European to USA frequency numbers.

I am delighted to at last have a pocket mp3 player with a great speaker. I can play all my MP3 voice downloads and improve my life, pocket carry it everywhere. Thank you Degen for being smart enough to solve my problems.

Microphone picks up best within a couple feet, and if used like that it provides clear sound. Even across the room you can still hear voices and sounds (although not as well as if you are close the the microphone) - they just sound far off in the distance.

Only complaint about the sound thus far is the volume. At least on one call I turned up my phone volume to the maximum and the speakerphone volume to the maximum and still had to listen with focus to the other person. Perhaps they were also on a cell phone? It was still very good quality sound, I just wish that I could have turned it up louder.

I also have had difficulty connecting with another cell phone. Tried to restart the other cell phone and the speakerphone a few times and still wouldn't recognize each other, so not sure what that's about - given the ease with connecting the first cell phone.

Given a couple issues I'm docking it one star, but it's pretty good overall.

The zip up soft travel case that it comes with is also a very nice plus!

reviews.title: A little pricey at $350, but 5 stars nonetheless
reviews.text:
I bought this speaker as well as a JBL Extreme 2 (ostensibly the same price, though I found the non-black JBL on sale for $200) I decided to keep the Audio Pro because I like the sound better. The JBL is no slouch mind you, but I preferred the the Audio Pro's sound quality, especially for vocals. I found the JBL's vocals to be just a bit thin.

Another benefit that the Audio Pro enjoys over the JBL is how they sound at lower volumes. The JBLs really want to be played loud, whereas the Audio Pro unit is perfectly happy at any volume.

Neither unit distorts at maximum volume. Speaking of maximum volume, both units get plenty loud enough to fill a good sized room, but will not fill your entire house with sound. It is interesting that the maximum volume is ABOUT the same for both, in spite of the amplifier power advantage enjoyed by the audio pro.

I am a ROON fan so I was very pleased that the Audio Pro can be used as a ROON endpoint via its AirPlay support. This is AirPlay 1 so resolution is limited to CD quality. Still that works fine for my use.

I have two minor complaints about the Audio pro:

1.) Portability: Unlike the JBL Extreme2, the This Audio Pro speaker needs to be plugged in to an AC outlet. (120v and 240v power chords are included, and there is no physical switch, so it must be auto-sensing) This could be a deal breaker for some.

2.) When moving the speaker (I use it in my office and in my shop), It takes it about 3 minutes before it is ready to be used. I think the time is used for searching for wifi connections. I do not know if making a physical (wired) connection using the Aux (headphone jack)/RCA/Ethernet inputs would fix this as I have not tried it. I actually called support when I first set this up, because I thought it might be defective.

3.) Related to my portability comment above, it is not outdoor friendly. (You can't get it wet, as you would expect from a device connected to the mains)
------

Note: I did confirm with Audio Pro that this unit is the same as the upcoming C10 MKII with the following exceptions:

1.) The MKII has a magnetically attached removeable grill. The cloth on the Drumfire is permanently affixed.

2.) The MKII will support Airplay 2 as well as Chromecast, so it should support higher resolution when using ROON

3.) Although U.S. Pricing has not been announced for the Addon C10 MKII, pre-order pricing in the UK is 500 quid, so I would expect a price point of around $500

Sound is good. Quite good. Very good. I am not an audiophile, but imho it's the best sound I have ever heard. Rich, juicy, loud, deep. No distortion that I can feel. Some files sound worse than others, but listen. The compression quality of the audio file plays a role, too.
Design is good. Looks modern, aesthetic, solid sturdy construction.
Now, it would never hold up for 20 hours. Under no circumstances. At most 5-6 hours in average, on medium volume.
Also, it did not connect correctly to my Alexa dot. After connection the dot and the speaker both remained silent. I was counting to use it with Alexa.
Finally, absence of AUX socket is a disadvantage. I would love to use the speaker with my old Zishan, but there is no way.
So, I will keep it to use with my cell for parties, but I am not completely happy with the features it offers.

reviews.title: Packs a punch for the size.
reviews.text:
I ordered the iHome Alexa Built-in Bluetooth Speaker Portable Wireless Waterproof Rechargeable Lights Up to Music, with Speakerphone, Passive Subwoofer, Carry Strap, Durable Shockproof Floatable Design (IBT158) to replace an old sub par portable speaker that I’ve had for years. The iHome is quite the upgrade with the built in Alexa, better sound and being waterproof. I’ve had this product now for several weeks and would like to share my thoughts.

I must say that the sound is pretty good and packs a punch in such a small size. It’s much better than the much smaller and several years old portable wireless speaker that I have been using. In fact there really is no comparison at all. Let’s just say that it is the best sounding portable wireless speaker that I personally have ever owned. My daughter who “borrowed” the older speaker some time ago (and she never gave it back) keeps asking to "borrow" the new iHome as she says, “it’s louder and sounds WAY better”. I absolutely agree with her. Plus the lights on this thing are a nice touch, and there are options (via a button on top) to cycle through and change the color options or turn them off.

Setting up the iHome for Bluetooth and Alexa was easy and very straight forward, and there has been no issues whatsoever. We are mainly an Android household however my oldest daughter uses an iPhone and everyone has had the same great experience. So far my only complaint is that the Bluetooth connectivity distance isn’t the greatest but with that said, none of my Bluetooth devices really have much range in our home so I am not going to knock points off for that. The sound out of this little guy makes up for the Bluetooth short comings and the bonus of Alexa being packed into this as well as the waterproof features make this a great value for the selling price.

One thing worth mentioning is that to use Alexa, you can’t just say “Alexa” to activate her. You do have to physically press a button on the iHome speaker to access her, which isn’t a huge deal breaker, but because of this, you can’t use other Alexa devices to make an announcement and have it broadcast to the iHome speaker. Being fairly new to the Alexa and smart home world, I am not going to hold this shortcoming against the iHome device. It actually makes sense that with this being portable, you wouldn’t want to have Alexa always listening and drain the battery while on the go. Speaking of Battery life, it's decent but not spectacular by any means. This is pretty subjective however as usually when I use the iHome, I'm listening to it at a pretty high volume ;)

Another observation is that this uses micro USB to charge, and I really would like to see more devices using the newer and better USB C charging capabilities.

As far as the “waterproof” capabilities go, I must report that I have yet to float the device in a pool or let the kids play with it outside while running through the sprinklers. I know that it says it’s waterproof and it absolutely looks like it would hold up to getting wet as it is very well built, rugged and quite solid, but I don't want to risk ruining this new toy that the whole family has been enjoying so much.

reviews.title: Every bike owner needs this.
reviews.text:
I have now owned my Zealot Bluetooth speaker/Light for over 3 months. It is quite a workhorse. I purchased this to replace my Photive Bike Speaker. The Photive introduced me to the luxury of having music safely while I biked, but it's mounting hardware made it unreliable and prone to falling off bracket.
That will definitely not be happening with the Zealot. It has a hard compressed thick plastic mount that fits tightly to the handlebar and the speaker screws on to it like a camera to a tripod, so it isn't falling off during a bump. BTW, you can also use it to mount a Go-Pro or similar camera that has screw mount. (I notice a lot of complaints about mounts breaking. It is a small fit and if you screw too tight the hinge pin can break. I would say the maximum circumference is about 3-1/2 inches. My handlebar is 3 inches and I use a spacer, so measure before considering. When installing do not over-tighten).
The light is super bright on high mode, that I can't even look into it without it blinding. It has three modes: Bright, Dim and Bright Flashing (S.O.S.). It is large in size like a hand-held flashlight and the silicone rubber covering makes it quite water-resistant. I have the sporty red color.
I ride my bike to work everyday in most conditions, except in extreme snow, and this holds up perfectly on the city streets. The speaker is just loud enough for personal enjoyment without annoying others. Granted, this will not be the speaker you will bring to the beach if you want to get a party started, but for personal use the sound is perfect. I even take it with me when I want to enjoy music while relaxing at the park, but not annoy others trying to relax. You can play music via Bluetooth, an SD card, or via FM radio, but for latter you must insert the charging cord to work as an antenna. Not a fan, as I don't like have a long cord dangling by my front wheel while biking.
I only use Bluetooth, so cannot reliably review other methods, except to say that SD works fine and you can use controls on speaker the same as you would use for Bluetooth (Volume, Next track, etc). FM is fine if you get good reception. Also, it does include an auxiliary cord if not using Bluetooth and USB charging cord in package. BTW, the packaging is beautiful, so it would make a great gift.
The battery lasts for a long time, about 10 plus hours of usage on a charge, and will hold a charge for days.
Most importantly, it is also a mobile power charger which most other Bluetooth bike speakers are not. I recently had my Iphone battery go down to 35 percent, and in 30 minutes of charging it brought it up to 65 percent. To get from 10 percent to 100 percent charge takes about and hour.
If you want to use it while hiking, it includes a Carabiner Clip that you can attach to a belt loop or knapsack loop for emergency lighting and music while traveling. (When you first unpack light, there will be a screw with a loop on the threads that you have to remove to screw on mounting bracket. Do not throw that screw away, that is where Carabiner will attach}. You can also take calls via Bluetooth if you don't want to access your phone, which I usually have in a jacket pocket or knapsack while biking.
So, in short - Great Bluetooth speaker, Water-resistant, a phone battery charger, a bright safety/emergency light, and a long charge. Perfect for the new generation of bikers.

reviews.title: Uniquely immersive sound & Alexa compatible
reviews.text:
This speaker really does fill the room with sound. It’s hard to explain, but it really does sound like the music somehow *in* the room rather than coming from a speaker in the room - if that makes sense. The sound easily fills regular sized rooms as well as large, high ceiling rooms. I thought that aspect was quite impressive.

You can make this super simple and easy to set up and use, or you can get more involved and be able to make customizations and add functionality like alexa.

If you want super simple - all you have to do is plug this in, press the power button then press the bluetooth button. Then find the speaker under the bluetooth available options on your phone and click it. Boom. Basic setup complete. Now you can play music from your phone through the speaker.

If you get the sony music center app on your phone, you are able to use the equalizer to adjust the different frequencies. This can make a really big difference. I would say even if you pump up the bass levels it is still a bit low on the bass - if you’re someone who loves music with a subwoofer, this won’t have enough for you (but also remember, it is *not* a subwoofer). And if you don’t like the immersive sound option (for some types of music I thought it made it sound a little muffled and the clarity wasn’t quite up to par) you can simply disable it and you re-enable it whenever you so choose. The app is so easy to use and takes about 1 minute to set it up. You don’t even need to make an account or anything on it. Just download the sony music center app, have your speaker turned on with bluetooth enabled and pretty much immediately you can be looking at and adjusting the sound settings. You can create your own custom equalizer settings or choose from the presets they have available (I’ve attached a photogrid with screenshots of using the app looking at these adjustments). With even minor alterations you can hear major differences.

If you want to use it with Alexa, first you need to have the sony music center app that I mentioned above installed. You do *not* do the Alexa setup in the alexa app, you do it in the sony music app. When I closed the sony app and reopened it, the setup for alexa automatically popped up. If it doesn’t, I’ve attached screenshots to show you how to find it (click on your speaker when you open the app, then click on settings, then click on network settings). It will walk you through connecting your speaker to your wifi and then allowing alexa voice access to your speaker. There’s even a step to name the speaker whatever you want (I just called mine “sony speaker”). Not too complicated once you know where to find the setup.

Now, it seems there’s confusion about what it means that this speaker works with alexa. It is NOT a replacement for an echo but it works WITH an echo. Think of it as similar to getting an alexa enabled light bulb or plug. You don’t yell at the bulb or plug to turn on or off. They don’t have microphones. You tell your amazon echo to turn on the light or turn off the plug. It’s the same with this speaker. Once you finish the above setup, you can now tell your echo (or your phone if you have alexa enabled on it) something like “alexa play my workout playlist on my sony speaker” and it will play your request on this speaker. And you will now also be able to see the speaker (whatever you named it during setup) under your list of connected devices on the amazon alexa app. You can also set it up with google home for basically the same functionality.

I like to blast my music while working out or dancing (or my newfound hobby of shuffling). With my custom equalizer settings, I was dancing around, enjoying the feeling of the sound reverberations on my skin and thought it was sounding quite good at high volume, but then my husband came in and said he thought it sounded muddled and lacked bass, especially when the volume was high. He did say it sounded pretty good at lower levels though. He’s the type that likes subwoofers and I do not, so everyone really does hear and prefer different frequency levels - you really can’t tell someone if what you’re hearing would please their ears or not. The automatic volume adjustments seem to work because I haven’t had to manually adjust the volume for different songs yet, so I’m keeping that enabled. Also I found it sounds better if I don’t have it too close to a wall. It can sound very different if you walk around the speaker in a circle, it seems different frequency levels come out at different volumes on different sides, so you may want to try turning it till you think it sounds best. It has on-board controls to skip to the next/previous song, volume, bluetooth, all the basics. Keep in mind this isn’t a battery-powered wireless speaker though, it does need to be plugged into an outlet to work.

I do think sometimes I hear a little bit of distortion in the lower frequency levels, but it’s possible that’s an unavoidable side effect of it being able to perform it’s impressive “room filling” music, I really can’t say but sure. But overall I would say I am pretty happy with how this sounds, and even more so with how it really does feel like you’re immersed with the music in the room. The unique way the sound is dispersed into the room really is a noticeable upgrade from our other speakers. Hope this helps you make a more informed decision!

reviews.title: Crystal clear, immersive sound!
reviews.text:
I wanted a home speaker with nice sound without a battery since it will be stationary most of the time. I also wanted an HD Bluetooth codec and line-in. Other popular "high end" brands, didn't bother to include the supported codec in their specs. This one supports AAC which is acceptable and supported by my Android phone. I wish it supported LDAC, but it's ok.

The sound is crystal clear, immersive and loud without any distortion/stress. Everything I was hoping for.

I mostly use it with Bluetooth, but you can cast using Spotify (and other apps that I didn't test/I don't use) and Wi-FI. When you do that, there is a lag between the Spotify App and the song playing on the speaker, so that's better to use when you don't plan fiddling and changing songs frequently through the app.

reviews.title: Fills the room with beautiful sound
reviews.text: I’m very pleased with this speaker. I set it up in my living room where I’m using it in place of a surround sound system and it fills that role well. I love that it has multiple ways of connecting to devices so it’s really easy to switch from the tv to somebody’s phone or tablet. This is the first speaker I’ve seen that offers both Bluetooth and WiFi connectivity. There’s also an audio jack for a physical connection. Controls are conveniently placed on top of the speaker.  Sound quality is exactly what I’ve come to expect from Sony. It’s excellent. The bass is deep and rich and the mid and high levels are clear and beautiful. You can customize the equalizer via the user friendly Music Center app. My favorite feature on this speaker is the 360 Reality Audio. Wow. It blew me away. I’ve listened to some nice speakers but never one that provided such a realistic experience. It is such a nice feature. I can crank it up and hear the music clearly throughout most of my home. It doesn’t distort at higher volumes either. I’m really enjoying this Sony speaker and highly recommend it.

reviews.title: WOW the sound is amazing!!!
reviews.text:
Prior to this speaker, I used the first gen Amazon Echo for my in-room sound. It suited my needs just fine, and I was very happy with it. Then I got the chance to try this, and now I realize why people spend a lot of money on speakers like these.

The speaker is very well made. All the controls are on the top, and they are labeled well. This speaker supports both Bluetooth and Wifi streaming. You can stream audio with the help of the Sony Music Center app. The speakers also support Chromecast for easy audio streaming via wifi.

The sound you get on these speakers is mind-blowing. I would not have thought you could get that quality of sound from speakers. And when paired with apps like Spotify, Amazon Music, and more, the sound is immersive and room-filling. You can also use these speakers with Alexa, and also there is the 360 Audio, which works with specific music services to provide even more spectacular sound.

I have these speakers connected via Bluetooth to my projector. Now I am getting room-filling, close-to-surround-sound on my video now. I would happily recommend these to anyone who wants a premium speaker. I have not head anything better.

reviews.title: Sounds Great But the App is Not Great
reviews.text:
Okay let's start with the basic set-up here. I have used the Sony 360 with both Amazon's Alexa, YouTube Music and Bluetooth. Two of those had a problem.

First the software that Sony tells you to install to get this speaker on Wi-Fi is installed as the Sony Music Center from the app store on Google, but is actually only called Music Center on the Android device. This small inconsistency should've prepared for me for things to come but... it didn't.

So you sign into Music Center, get your device online, easy so far, and then name. Next came the nightmare of getting Alexa to see the device. It just wouldn't it. I am not kidding, it took four or five tries to get Alexa to see it, and then I decided to rename the device because even though the speaker is large, it's not so large that you don't want to carry it from say upstairs to down stairs, like I do. It's not portable in the true sense of the word (requires a plugin), but it's not that heavy. So then I renamed it... Music Center and Alexa don't seem to syn the names at all, so the old name is on the Music Center app and both names are on Alexa... okay, whatever.

From there, the shortcomings come from Alexa mostly because she refuses to play my playlist half the time and wants to use Alexa's public lists... no thank you. It's just clunky at this point, not prohibitive, but what is odd is when you have your playlist going and all of sudden what speaker and phone don't show the same song playing. I just want to skip a song, but it likes to restart as if the speaker and phone don't realize they're not connected any longer. I mean it's a smart speaker, so relying 100% of the phone is probably not wanted, but it's not exactly independent either so... not ideal.

Now we move to Google Music. YT Music you say, because we all know Google Music is gone... yeah but this Sony Speaker doesn't know that. It ships with Google Music which flat out doesn't work, so I had to do a little searching to find out how to get YT Music on there which was a little awkard too consider the speaker software is expecting you to use Play Music which was retired. Heck I even updated the firmware thinking that might help... nope. So yeah the instructions don't actually work because it's reliant mostly on one defunct app.

Okay, Chromecast itself is not something I use every often. I find it clunky and not great. I mean most my smart devices have built in apps so why bother right? I'm telling you this because even though I have an Android phone and a Goggle Hub and even had a Google Hockey Puck for a minute, I largely just use the Hub to look up recipes and ask quick questions in the kitchen. I still don't like Chromeast. I mean it might even be the reason for the desync between the phone and the speaker playlist; it won't let me cast free music to the speaker, that requires a premium service apparently, so I mostly play my lists of tracks I paid for. I know right. People still do that!

Once it was set-up, it works about 90% of the time. I mostly go to Alexa and do my playlists because my playlists are YT Music aren't as current, but sometimes I just need to play some Kung Fu Panda.

I am not an audiophilia individual by any stretch of the imagination, but all my TVs have either a sound bar or are set-up to a speaker. I have around a dozen little bluetooth speakers, and I am not getting I have a half dozen if not more headsets for the PC, a Blue Yeti Nano, surround system for the gaming PC, and several bluetooth headphones (good ones). I do care about sound, but I also don't mind streaming music and MP3s so... there you are.

I think anyone with any sort of tech troubleshooting skills, and not great ones by the way, just, you know, anyone who approaches tech devices with more than "How do I get The GOOOGLE to work?" question will figure this out. It's just not as smooth as it should be.

The buttons on the devices, and yes those are button s on the top, work well. The light indicator are excellent. It really does tell you exactly how you are connected with a glance, raise or lower volume, pause... and you can do that via the phone too. It does fill the room nicely. I hear bass, like real bass. It's not going to replace my standalone subwoofers or anything like that, but it has some ummph to it which I like. Working from home, it's also really handy to be able to just open the phone and pause the music.

So overall, it's a nice speaker with decent tech backing it but the user experience really needs a bit of a reboot. I mean even when I registered the thing, I couldn't figure out what model I had... no, no not that model. You see they have a black and brown one and this grey and white one, and each of those is a different model but it's not actually on the machine or on the box so I just... guessed, and chose poorly. It's 2021 so if they're going to make use pick our model including the color... show the picture. Just store a tiny image on your website alongside the usual information on where to find your unit's information. Great news is... apps, user experience, registration websites all that can be fixed! and I hope they do that.

reviews.title: Small, but mighty!
reviews.text:
My wife and I already have a couple of Bluetooth speaker systems, one is kind of large and very powerful, and the other is what I would call mid-sized (but still sounds great). We wanted to get a small one, but one which still produced loud and high-fidelity sound. It's hard to locate the perfect speaker when looking online, so relying on reviews helps a lot. When I first saw this Raymate Bluetooth speaker on Amazon, however, it didn't even have any reviews (apparently being a new item on the market). But I liked that it had a rated output power of 20W, so I knew it would be loud enough; plus it was about the size we were looking for. So I took a chance on the unknown aspect of how good the sound might be and ordered it even without reviews.

When the package arrived I was happy to notice that at least the box that contained the speaker was pretty hefty. Where speakers are concerned, heft usually translates to bigger magnets in the speakers, which typically means better sound with good power handling. I really wanted to hear how this sounded, so I paired it to a cell phone right away even before charging it. It paired easily and quickly (pairing mode was already enabled by default upon initial power-on). Then I started a song playing on the phone and WOW! Both my wife and I were thrilled by the quality and power of the sound! It sounded a lot like my mid-sized bluetooth speaker which has a bigger case and larger speaker components than this one. Really nice! There was just the right amount of Bass: smooth and just powerful enough to add that nice foundation for the tone without being overpowering. The mids and highs were clear and accurate, with nice sizzle from cymbal crashes. I would categorize the sound as very well-balanced and true-to-life, particularly when the front of the speaker is positioned to point directly at you.

There are membrane-style buttons on the top panel for power, volume plus and volume minus, as well as a play/pause button and a mode button which enables re-pairing and other functions depending on how long you keep the button pressed. As a matter of fact, all the buttons likewise have multiple functions in this way, all of which is clearly explained in the included instruction manual. While paired to a phone, you can receive or reject phone calls through the speaker (it has a built-in mic). On one end of the speaker body there is a flip-out hanging bracket, while the other end sports a waterproof rubber cover which protects the device's ports. There is a USB-C port for charging, a 3.5mm jack for audio input from non-bluetooth devices, and even an SD card slot. You can load a bunch of songs on an SD card (with up to 64GB capacity) for playing through this speaker. Four different popular audio file formats are supported, including MP3 and WAV.

This speaker also supports TWS, which allows you to wirelessly connect two TWS-enabled speakers together to provide true stereo sound. That is, one of the speakers plays mono left-channel sound, while the other plays mono right-channel sound. With the two separated by the appropriate amount depending on their distance from you, they provide a full-stereo soundstage. Nice feature!

There really isn't anything about this speaker that I don't like. It's solidly built, doesn't take up a lot of room, sounds great, generates a lot of sound, and has great extra features built-in. What's not to like? All this at what I consider to be a very reasonable price. A solid five-star item if ever there was one!

reviews.title: Shaker and wireless charging work well - other features are just adequate

So far, it's been working well for getting him up without a parent having to do it and without waking the rest of the house.  The shaker is very strong and hard to ignore.  The build quality of the clock is adequate for a device at this price point, but not that impressive - the display looks nice, but the buttons have a cheap feel and click loudly.  The unit is lightweight but does stay put well enough due to grippy rubber feet.  The LED display has two brightness settings plus off.  The audio quality of the radio isn't too hot... it's mono and hollow sounding with no bass, really only passable for news or talk radio.  The wireless phone charging and shaker are the key features I bought the unit for, and both work well.  Note that you can only set each of the two alarms to shaker OR beeper OR radio, no combinations.  To get a combo, maybe you could use both alarms, set to a time where they'd overlap..?

reviews.title: Great sound in a small package!
reviews.text: Bought several wireless bookshelf sized speakers to run from my desktop iMac (or iPhone/ iPad if I wished) for my office/man-cave to test head-to-head. I recently finished a complete room make-over, installing solid wood paneling and acoustic tiles and setting up to double as a music room for listening and recording. So needless to say, I was going to be very picky. Had never heard of Audio Pro, but saw some recent reviews and added their C10 to the mix. It easily blew the other competitors away (JBL, Sony, Bose). The sound quality is outstanding across a wide range of music tastes. Clear, articulate highs, crisp mids without being muddy, and really impressive bass for so small a box. It will definitely rock. For me, to get things sounding right for any room and your listening style, using an equalizer (iTunes / Music in this case on either my IOS devices or on my iMac) is a must. I also love being able to move the C10 around to different places easily without all the wires! I've now used it in a couple different rooms and even outside once. The style/look is very attractive: modern, clean, pro looking. I've had a number of people comment: "All that is coming from that little lunch-box with the handle?? Wow!!"

reviews.title: It's a nice clean looking unit and prefers 2.4 ghz network for wifi
reviews.text:
Make sure you use 2.4 ghz wifi for less hassle. Doesn't like 5 ghz but will work if you don't mind redoing wifi signal everytime you unplug unit, which was my experience so finally put home wifi on 2.4 and it never loses network connection. This could be fixed with firmware update I'm sure.

It's a nice clean looking unit..Sound quality probably won't blow you away (tested lossless wifi only) but for small speaker not bad. Treble highs suffer the most IMO, not really close to the soundbar ZVOX Audio SB500 I was comparing next too. It does get loud at 80 watts total RMS and bass is on boomy side.
The Zvox soundbar isn't portable plus big and heavy so wasn't comparing apples to apples here, just saying its not gonna be mind blowing
audio with such a small package. My primary home system is Klipsch so you can tell I like a speaker that leans more on the bright side and this one doesn't.

Edit after a full week I'm little disappointed. Can't get use to the fact base is overdone. Sound quality is just okay for the sticker price, just too much bass for my liking so downgraded to 3 stars.

reviews.title: Good for emergencies
reviews.text: I selected this radio to keep with the rest of our emergency supply kit. If you'd like to do the same, I'd recommend you charge the radio first before putting it away. You'll be working the hand crank for hours if you don't, and that's no fun if the power is out. Sound works pretty well, the light works great too. You'll want to hang onto the instruction because the buttons for the radio are not intuitive. I like how it has a usb output if you need to recharge your phone, but I too wish there was a storage area for the charging cable. I don't get a lot of direct sun where I am, so I don't think the solar panel would be that helpful for me, especially if there's a storm that knocks out the power. For the price though, I think this radio would be a good addition to your emergency kit.

reviews.title: Brings joy to relative with Alzheimer's
reviews.text: [[VIDEOID:764ab20e42e49b7d27a2933732472e1b]] Mom loves music.  But, we struggle with earbuds because she will take them out and lose them.  She likes to wrap up electrical cords really tight which destroys them.  So, then we tried connecting this headset to an old iPad.  See the video.  Jamming to music transforms her from being tired and restless to dancing and signing.  We love how it surrounds her with music, so there is nothing in her ears and so that we don't have to listen to the same music that she likes to hear.  And, she will listen to it for longer than earbuds, likely because she feels the buds in her ear canal and because they either fit snug or they fall out.  We take the iPad with us in the car to get sunshine and a little peace.  And it's cool that, she might not remember the last 10 years, but she'll sing along to songs from 40 years ago that we have never heard of and will jam to others.  We transformative experience of surrounding of these personal surround sound bluetooth speakers!

But I'll be honest, after trying these, I'm not really loving them. I had a pair of sunglasses speakers that aimed sound towards my ears, but this sort of blasts sound out and around me. Like, not even towards my ears. Basically, it seems just as loud to someone else in the room with me as it does to me, which then begs the question of why not just use an external speaker at that point? The call quality was just OK as well. The one thing I can say is that the build quality seems quite good. It feels really durable and made with premium feeling materials. But I just can't shake the feeling that for the asking price, I'm missing the point of these. Shouldn't the speakers be facing upwards towards my ears instead of blasting at each other in front of my Adam's Apple? Seems like a weird design that might be missing the mark.

reviews.title: A different way of enjoying audio
reviews.text:
This is the first neckband headset that I have owned. I love to listen to audio but many times wearing headphones becomes uncomfortable after awhile due to to the headphones irritating my ears, or the headband not fitting right. In addition they can get warm and cause you to sweat, which is very unpleasant. Some are much better than others, but I wanted to have an alternative that I could wear that would not have these issues.

I have tried bone-conduction headphones with little success. I thought that these headphones were like that at first, but when I read the full description I was interested in giving the headphones a try. The packaging that the neckband comes in is good. The neckband headphones use a USB-C connection, which is fantastic. I am glad to see more peripherals starting to use this type of connector over mini-USB.

The neckband is easy to use. Just charge it and then press the round circular button to turn it on and start the pairing process. I got these to connect to my cell phone right away and I started to use them. I was surprised at the sound quality. It is ok, considering there are no earcups that sit on your ears. Of course, with no earcups this means that others nearby can hear your audio, so these offer less privacy than standard headphones. If you don't mind that then, the sound is pretty good. It does feel surround-like, but the quality is more than acceptable. The connection works well for me and I don't get any drops.

So the main thing is that others can hear your audio so you will have to manage the volume if you want privacy. But if you are ok with that, then these neckband headphones are great. They are made of a rubberized material that is super comfortable and they never get slick with a greasy feel. The neckband is not adjustable but unless your neck is the size of a tree trunk then they will fit and stay on securely. The only other quibble I have is that the skip and seek buttons are the same, so it can take awhile to get the feel of the difference between seeking on the same track and switching to the next track. Also, the neckband does not have any built-in volume control for the audio. This means that you must adjust the volume on the audio source, which is a curious omission.

I like these headphones and I am liking them the more and more I use them. I wish there was volume control and the sound could be better, but for the price these are a great product and I would happily recommend these if you want to spare your ears the discomfort associated with earcups when you listen to audio.

reviews.title: Impressive Sound from an Easy to Use Convenient Speaker
reviews.text:
I have tested and reviewed literally hundreds of Bluetooth speakers and while I am not a fan of music that is particularly bass heavy I found this speaker produces rich, vibrant sounds from all wave lengths. It produces more than ample volume for most any setting and has several connection methods.

While I have tested and reviewed Bluetooth speakers costing ten times (and more) what this does, the sound quality from this speaker is really quite good. In relation to the sound quality I would place them on par with mid to high end Bluetooth speakers.

In regards to charging time and battery life, both are outstanding. In my tests charging takes about approximately 2 hours to charge the built in 4000 mAh battery and the speaker lasts a solid 4.5 hours at max volume - 8 hour with volume midway (of course this will vary a bit due to exact settings).

There are multiple ways to connect to this speaker including Bluetooth 5.0, which can reach much further than previous versions, through an AUX cable, a 3.5mm jack, TF card, USB flash drive, or FM radio - it even has a built in extendable antenna.

While it has a remote and I tested it and it works fine, I rarely use it as I connect with my phone all the time.

I have taken this speaker with me to the pool for the last couple of months and have been thoroughly impressed with its performance. The battery, being 4000 mAh, is much longer lasting than most allowing for all day listening and the sound quality has been really good.

This is an all around great Bluetooth speaker that I certainly recommend.
