The woofers deliver solid bass, and the directions really help fill a space with sound. I love that it even has a carrying handle and a place to plop your phone onto (great for Karaoke!). I'm a little confused by the Mic input, I thought perhaps this could work as an alternative to the line in... for example, I can line in for music, but also sometimes I'd like a mic-level input for using with a microphone. But the mic input seems to only get used for some sort of recording to TF card function, which I couldn't get to work anyway. Doesn't matter, I wasn't so interested in that feature, I was more interested in using it as an amp and thought that might be an interesting alternative use.
Using the speaker for both bluetooth audio or wired aux in worked very well. The FM radio is nice too, but I didn't try it much. All in all, the battery life seems pretty solid and this thing is incredibly powerful for a battery operated speaker. We usually don't max out the volume because that's too loud!

reviews.title: Really great sound!
reviews.text:
This product had something missing I was looking for - an aux input jack. Unfortunately, no. The light was not all that bright, but still useful. I gave it a 4-star for these two reasons.

The box is first class - you will want to keep it to store the unit when not in use. I had a little trouble figuring out how to open it, until I saw the little yellow tab sticking out, and checked the box construction so I would pull in the right direction.

The speaker/light is contained in a canvas bag, which can be attacked to a strap for backpacking. While I don't think the speaker is waterproof, it certainly seems well made and a little water on it should not be a problem. Keeping it in the canvas bag would help if it rains.

The speaker/light itself feels very well made, with a nice surface finish. It looks like it can take some rough experiences and still work fine. Of course I have not tried to test this by throwing it over a cliff and seeing if it still works... :)

The instructions, as usual these days, are tiny and hard to read. And somewhat unclear. It took me quite a while to understand that the M was the mode button, which at first I did not realize was a button at all.

It was easy to connect to my phone via Bluetooth and play music right away. The light worked from the get-go, and I discovered later how to turn it on and off. The speaker is always on when the unit is powered up, and so is the light, so turning the light off is forgotten during a power cycle.

It takes forever for the unit to shut off. I start to think - maybe I am not pressing the button hard enough, or something? I think it takes 5 seconds or more. That seem a little silly. Maybe they are trying to make it child proof. It is almost me-proof.

There is a MODE button, play/stop, volume up/down, next and previous song (holding down buttons longer) on top, around the LED brightness control. There is also the light on/off and the LINK button, for using with multiple speakers. The MODE button has an LED on it, as does LINK, but I am unclear about when they are lit. MODE seems to always be lit. I have no interest in multiple speaker use, so I am ignoring them. I think MODE is used for controlling multiple speakers, connected using LINK, but not sure. Ah, for better, BIGGER instructions!

The sound - both volume and overall sound quality and bass is very nice. The cary handle is also very helpful, and this will do well as a camp device. I wish they used a separate ON/OFF for speaker and light.

The light is designed to shine most light downward - to a table surface, for example, and shield your eyes from direct LED light. It is soft white light, and not super bright, but useable.

It was hard for me to find the charging and done charging LED - in a tiny hole above the power switch. The charging port is hidden under a flap, so on first glance, it is not obvious where it is.

This also acts as a charger for your phone. The USB output connector is located under the same flap as the charging microUSB connector, as well as what looks like a memory card slot. I would guess that you can plug in a card and play from it. Another use for the MODE switch, switching between Bluetooth and internal memory card.

So, interesting design, not perfect, but a really nice unit overall.

reviews.title: Great gift for yourself, or someone else
reviews.text:
[[VIDEOID:33a32e99b2ed7a62d09f52bb9977e28d]] I love this camping lantern/speaker. It's incredibly high quality; boxing and presentation are top-notch; and the sound, look, and feel of it are excellent.

The overall quality plus the packaging are the reason I say it would make a great gift. It was a pleasure just opening this. The sturdy box is nicely designed, and has little magnetic closures. The bag for the speaker is high quality and looks cool. And the speaker/light itself is just amazing.

I especially love that this has a warm light mode. The amber color is gorgeous. That's not something you find in most camping lanterns. It does have a cool white mode but I definitely prefer the amber. And there is a dial on top for stepless dimming. Even that dial has a smooth action that speaks to the quality of this product.

This speaker is louder, with better sound quality, than any other 20 watt speaker I have, and also better than a pair of 10 watt speakers I have. At full volume I could not hear any noticeable distortion, and at all volumes it had a very nice bass quality. Great sound spectrum, from high to low frequencies.

While the description says this will play music for 30 something hours, the caveat to that is that manufacturers always say that depends on various factors. The main factor is your volume. At full volume the battery lasted 8 and a half hours streaming music from my iPad. For a party you might have this cranked up full blast for a few hours, but if you're using it camping or something like that, you'll probably use it at half or lower volume, and the battery will last very long time. Speaking of parties, this would be great for a gathering of maybe a dozen people. If you really want sound for 50 people who want to dance, this is not the speaker for you. I've hosted events like that, and we use a 60 watt speaker. This would not cut it for that kind of party, but it's a camping lantern/speaker, not a sound system for a rager.

I doubt I would ever use this as a power bank, because it's too useful on its own. But it would charge my phone from 0 to 100% at least twice.

reviews.text:
Two week update: I took away a star because I found something that goes way beyond annoying... The low battery warning. Instead of just fading away, or beeping once, and maybe sending a signal to the device it's linked to, it beeps. The beep is MUCH louder than the volume I listen to at night... And it doesn't stop. Just keeps going, every few seconds.

Due to the problems it has with the sensitivity (or lack) of the volume, I placed the speaker a good distance from my bed. When the battery started dying, it obviously woke me, and by the time I got up, turned off the speaker, convinced my dogs that the beeping did not indicate an intruder in the house, and their barking was not helpful, then crawled back into bed... I couldn't fall asleep again.

If you have trouble sleeping, find a speaker you can use while it charges, or one that at least has a power meter, so that you're not jolted awake.

I am reasonably pleased with this little speaker. The sound is aggressively average in quality. The bass is (obviously) the weak point, and the volume goes from a little too loud for nights (or most business offices), to "please go get my hearing aid" near silence. The sound gets a little tinny when you go louder, for whole room sound.

The battery life isn't too bad. I've only had this a few days, so I can't say anything regarding longevity for the time it holds a charge.

I do appreciate the little travel case it came with. The tennis ball color is horrifying, and the dogs think it's a toy, but it does protect the speaker.

Hopefully newer versions of this will have a more discreet power indicator, or none at all. The blue light is VERY bright.

reviews.title: Great "In-The-Middle" Speaker.  Not too small...Not too large.
reviews.text:
1 3.75
 
Bang & Olufsen offer a variety of portable speakers. This is the “middle-of-the-road” speaker. Meaning it’s not the smallest, but not the largest. Their smallest is the Beoplay P2 which will fit in the palm of your hand. Great for a desk, and when you want a speaker so small you can fit it into your pocket. But it doesn’t have the power / sound for larger spaces. The large Beolit 17 is a “party-in-a-box” kind of speaker for full-sound on a patio. .. but. . it’s much larger and not something you can put in a backpack. This Beosound A1 is what “fits in the middle”. It’s small enough to put it into a backpack. It gives a nice amount of power / sound for a small group on a beach. . . dorm room. . . and so on.

I also have the 1st generation A1, so I’m familiar with this speaker. The A2 has some nice upgrades. First of all, it’s now waterproof. Up to 1 meter of water for 30-minutes. So you can use it in the shower. . .by the pool. . .or at the beach without a problem. BUT. . . The speaker comes with a leather strap. It looks great, but if you’re going to be getting this speaker wet a lot, then you might want to change the strap.

Another thing they have improved on are the buttons. On the first edition, you didn’t “feel” anything when you pressed them, so it was hard to know if anything was happening or not. Now you feel the “click”. Having said that. . . . because the buttons are around the edge, you still have to hold the speaker. . . turn it around. . . and find the button you want to press. Honestly, that’s kind of annoying. But you can also use the B&O app to operate the speaker. The app also gives you options for different listening “styles” and such.

You can also set the speaker up to use with Alexa, if you have it.

This speaker works very well as a speakerphone as well. If you’re going to use it as a speakerphone, you’ll want to go into the B&O app and select “Speech” as the “listening mode”.

This speaker is not light. It has a weight of 1-pound 3.75oz. But it’s a much more robust small speaker than other. . . lighter. . . cheaper. . . speakers of the same size. This speaker measures 5.25” across and 2” high.

This speaker comes in two colors. . Anthracite (black) and Grey Mist (silver). They are under different listings.

The base of the speaker is kind of “rubbery”. It’s kind of “anti-slip”, but it is almost smooth, so it will still slide down something at a sharp angle.

Though there is a “flashing light” on the speaker to let you know the battery status. . . The easiest way to check is through the B&O app.

After receiving, and downloading the app, there will probably be a firmware update for the speaker. This took about a half-hour to install.

Made in China.

reviews.title: Nicest/Most Expensive Mat I've ever purchased
reviews.text:
I have recently stepped up my yoga practice and I wanted a comfortable mat. My old mat was a basic thin Gaiam mat that served it's purpose on hardwood floors, but I needed something that wouldn't slide and bunch up on carpet.

When researching for the best mat I could buy, I came across three that were contenders: the Manduka Prolite, the Manduka Pro, and the Jade Harmony. I decided to purchase the Prolite because it is non-latex, lighter than the Pro, and has a great warranty. The Jade Harmony was not latex free (I have an allergy) and didn't include a lifetime warranty.

I purchased the Thrive color in 71'. The color is a deeper emerald green and I really like the color against the black logo. As for the length, I am 5'7 and I find that the extra few inches make a difference in my practice. The cushion and support this mat offers is better than I have ever experienced with any of my five prior $20 mats. Further, it is pretty light and I could definitely take this to a studio when not practicing at home.

My mat arrived in fine condition but with a little indent from where the label was. Given the price, I was annoyed but I let it go. I jumped on the mat quickly after I opened it to test out the slippage and I really didn't experience anything more than I have on my prior mats. In down dog, I do feel my hands slide slightly, but I know with time (or a salt treatment), this should wear away. (Should it not, I will update my review). I was SUPER nervous based on other reviews about slipping during practice, but I just completed a 20 min. intermediate vinyasa flow with no issues.

One tip I have is DO NOT store the mat in a wire basket. I stored it rolled-up and vertical in a wire basket and the bottom end (the edges of the mat) became a little dented from the pressure.

I would definitely re-purchase but I would probably shop around on price. While this color was on sale, there are other colors elsewhere that are even cheaper. For that reason, I give four stars. This mat is great, but it didn't blow my mind. (I am hoping to update this review to 5 stars should my mind change through practice).

reviews.title: Takes time to break in but it's worth it
reviews.text: I bought this a month ago after lots of research between this and the jade mat. I ended up going with this and was prepared to wait for it to break in. The first few tries were rough, the mat was really slippery. I washed it with dish soap and sea salt, scrubbed it and hosed it off and left it to dry in the sun. That seemed it help a bit but it still was slippery. I usually bring a little towel to class to wipe my sweat so I used that to wipe my hands on I would just put it under my hands so they wouldn't slip. Today I took a class and it was better. A little slippery but much better then it was. I think it will only get better with time. Maybe I'll give another review in a few weeks! Definitely reccomend though. It's awesome. Really sturdy and comfy.

reviews.title: Worth it
reviews.text: I love this mat! First of all, I'm glad it's less expensive than I originally planned to spend on a Manduka mat. Second of all, it's good and sticky. Very sturdy and heavy (in a good way). It's not going anywhere and neither am I--meaning, the mat doesn't move once you put it down and my feet are planted and not slipping when in my asanas. It didn't stink more than any other mat when I first got it. It's only been a few weeks and I don't smell a thing (and I did nothing to it). I haven't taken any hot or sweaty yoga classes to see how it holds up in one of those but I have a yoga mat towel just in case. Glad I bought this. reviews.title: I highly recommend--especially for the older exerciser.
reviews.text:
First, I have to admit that I am not one of those people who loves to exercise. Any excuse will do to get me out of it. One of my most useful has been that hard surfaces hurt an old injury in my tailbone. Neither the bath mats I used at first, nor the thin and useless exercise mat I got later helped to make me feel either comfortable or secure.

This mat fortunately (or unfortunately, depending on how you look at it) removes that particular excuse. First, it is at least twice (probably even more than three times) as thick as the previous one I had. Secondly, the non-slip surface has a raised surface, a hill-and-valley design, that creates insulating air pockets that I appreciate, even on my unforgivingly hard tile or marble floors. (Supposedly, it's 3/8th of an inch, but I measure 1/2 inch on the "hill" parts). I'm not saying it's soft--it's not, I'm still exercising on a firm surface, but there is a significant difference when I'm flat on the floor whether I'm on my back, sides, on my knees, or upright. I don't feel the need to put a towel over it, like I did with my other mat, when lying down, and I feel very stable and secure when standing. I feel firmly grounded and don't constantly reach for something to hold on to.

Due to my age, I don't do anything very strenuous, I just work on flexibility and stability, I do exercises with small weights, repetitive joint strengthening exercises, and a lot of stretching and reaching. I've never done anything on this mat that involves jumping or using weights heavier than 5 lbs each, but the build and integrity of the mat suggests to me that it would hold up under much more intense conditions than those I subject it to. It also cleans very easily and I expect that it will be very durable.

The only problem I can see--and it doesn't affect me because I only use it at home--is rolling it back up to the size it originally came in, which is how it will fit back into the elastic carrier. If you're going to be taking it places, I hope you're much more coordinated than I am. (Actually, that isn't hard.)

reviews.title: Very thick, stays put on slick floors
reviews.text: This mat appears to actually be two different mats sealed together. The bottom one is black and ridged for traction against the floor. The top one is purple and smooth for exercise etc. I tried it on a slick tile floor, carpeted area and the slick wood floors. Stretching, light yoga and even jumping jacks did not dislodge it on any of the floor types - the traction held and the mat stayed put. It's thick and soft, but not mushy when you kneel on it and it feels good on bare feet. I also like the little harness thing with the handle - just roll the mat up, slip the elastic loops over each end and it's ready to go.

reviews.title: Loving this Mat 5yrs Later.
reviews.text:
UPDATE 9/28/15 (Yes, I am still using this product):

This is for those looking for a mat that is not a yoga mat, this is not a yoga mat and is a lot thicker than a yoga mat, it is a thick corrugated exercise mat.

I have used this mat for just about every kind of stretched or strength training exercises. I mainly do martial arts and dance, and you do pretty intensive stretching and resistance exercises using your own body weight, for both. I love this mat because I do not have carpet in my living room, but rather laminate flooring, so it provides more than enough cushioning.

Heck, I have even slept on this, and while it wasn't extremely comfortable, its better than sleeping on a hard surface. I am not saying I recommend it, but it was worth noting. I still use this mat at least twice a week, it's very thick and dense, and hasn't shown any signs of wear at all. The only drawback is the "carrier" it comes with is not much of a carrier, but a very flimsy piece of elastic. :(

ORIGINAL REVIEW originally from 2011:

Had a few exercise and/or yoga mats, and a lot of times they aren't much better than exercising on the floor. This one is very thick and it is soft while still firm, but not obnoxiously thick, the bottom is ribbed, so I think that helps it feel thicker without being extremely thick, it helps the impact of your body be cushioned it seems. Done various exercises on it, stretches, pilates, and some of my custom exercises, and it didn't hurt my hip like it normally would on a hard surface or even sometimes on a carpet, so that is nice. The carrying strap is a nice additions well as none of my other mats have even had that, makes it a lot more convenient to carry around. :D

God Bless ~Amy

reviews.title: Great at First, But Not Durable Enough for Regular Use
reviews.text:
I really loved this mat at first. Yes, it was a little slick and smelly, as most new mats are, but after scrubbing with vinegar solution and letting it sit for a few days, the smell and residue were gone. The mat is soft and supportive, a good size for a taller person (I'm 5'11"), and non-toxic. The only drawback was that it was always kind of slick if my hands were sweaty (a problem in an 85 degree ashtanga studio - I can't even imagine doing hot yoga on this).

But after a few months, it began to shred where my feet are in a downward dog. It's been about 5 or 6 months of 3-5 practices a week, and dime-sized chunks are now missing. I leave class with blue plastic lint all over my pants and under my toenails (which I keep trimmed, thankyouverymuch).

In short, if you're doing a more relaxed style of yoga on a hard wood floor, this might be a nice cushy mat for you; it certainly feels great for savasana. But it is not durable under regular use, and it is not appropriate for a sweaty class.

reviews.title: excellent alternative to plastic

i needed to replace my old yoga mat, which rats ate holes in when it was stored in the garage... i trimmed the eaten bits, but was left with something a bit too short for my workout, though good size for the beach!

i wanted to get a replacement mat that was not made from plastic, but options were limited. cork was interesting, but still backed with plastic...

i found this mat and decided to give it a shot. after my first workout on it, i am very pleased with my purchase so far!

what i like: 100% cotton, thick sturdy weave (similar to my rug under it actually!), feels durable, bright colors, stays put while i move, grippy texture.

what i don't like: smells a little musty (but i'm sure that'll air out if i put it in the sun for a couple hours), a little rough on the hands (just not as plush as plastic mats, but it's fine), and lastly unsure what the coating on the base is (the coating under the mat is very effective at keeping the mat in place while you workout, on carpet or on the hard floor, but i wish i knew what it was.. is it plastic? glue? it's got an almost waxy texture, i hope it's natural and not micro plastics but i'm not certain - any info from the manufacturer would be great!)

anyway i think this is an awesome mat for someone that wants to avoid plastic, it looks great and always nice to be a little more earth friendly. it's not as soft as foam mats, but it's fine (esp if you are using it on carpet).

reviews.text:
NOTE: I received a free sample of this knee pad to review.

I practice yoga regularly and am currently about midway through a yoga teacher training program. I own several mats, with the one I use the most often being [[ASIN:B009LHXD3O Manduka EKO Lite]]. This mat is on the thin side--which I generally like--and yet there are times when I find a bit of extra padding to be supportive.

The length of the SukhaMat worked so that it fit across my entire yoga mat. The width seemed a bit narrow, as I found myself adjusting the placement of the pad during use. As promised, the mat definitely did provide cushioning, yet I found the density of the mat to be a bit too much on the "squishy" side rather than providing firm support. And although the mat is supposedly made of foam, I found that it gave off a bit of an unpleasant, rubbery scent.

In the end, I didn't find this mat to be more convenient than standard yoga props such as blankets or blocks. Even rolling it up with my yoga mat for storage/transport was a problem--when I did this, it made my yoga mat too bulky, and it caused the SukhaMat to curl up on the edges rather than to lie flat. I can't say that this mat worked well for me, but it may be better for others who are in need of a more cushy product.

reviews.title: Nice mat- read below to be sure it will fit your sizing needs..!!!
reviews.text:
This mat is nice quality for the price.. it would be great for any beginner for sure! The length is where you need to be sure you get the right/good fit- and this mat is 6 feet long. This may seem plenty big, especially for someone like me as, I’m 5’1”..!! However, keep in mind… Is the movement and stretches you’ll be doing while on your mat! And for those much taller then, my 5ft self- this may pose a bit of a problem by not providing enough length..
•Best way to avoid getting a mat that is too short-
is to raise arms to a relaxed stance above head.. then, add that measurement to your total height- (from top if head to end of palms- add on these inches- not entire arms length!!) this will insure you’ll fit on your mat during all sun salutations and downward dogs! Makes sense.. But, something I hadn’t realized when ordering. Even so, @ 5ft. tall and reach of my arm still left me approx 4+” to spare- But, something to definitely be aware of when selecting!
•Strap is easy to put on and is all one piece-
Assemble in elastic material and has reinforced stitching to avoid breaking. **dont throw it away!! The strap was loose in bottom of box- and if you don’t look thoroughly, it could easily make it out to the trash- mine did!! But, once I realize it was missing I retraced my steps and found it on the bottom of the tubed boxed! Just pat attn.- this IS NOT placed on mat when it arrives!!! **Bonus: I LOVE the length of the strap.. not too long to bounce around your knees and get in the way when carried- This strap offers just enough slack to carry of the shoulder perfectly- I attached photos.. and this is perfect length!!! (length is NOT adjustable!)

•Not all mats are created equal! BUT.. A thinner mat is not always a bad thing. I did order one with extra thickness before.. tbh, it’s very “grabby” on the feet.. This is thinner so, yes! You may feel pressure points on the floor a bit more however, this mat allows for easy movement with the feet- I loved the textured surface- it helps keeps feet from becoming sweaty and slipping!
• I have used the mat a handful of times.. and maybe OCD about disinfecting after every use, I don’t care! I use a misting mat cleaner that is all natural.. I spray both sides with a light coat. So far, we’ve held up just fine! No sticky or, peeling of the mat itself- **the key here people: to let cleaner dry before rolling/storing your mat!!! Here’s a Life hack: whenever you clean your mat, always be sure it’s 100% dry before rolling/storing! You will thank me for this and mats life expectancy will last much longer than you think! Not too mention, you won’t be the one who’s mat stinks up the room for the whole class.. that’s always a good thing!!
Overall, this is a great mat and good investment for any who need a clean, nice, decent space to do their exercises- it may not have all the added extras but, for many... those are just that, extra!
I can recommend this feeling confident it can do it’s job and one will get their moneys worth.
I hope this info helps.. feel free to let me know!

I debated getting a different mat to replace it - manduka, jade, lulu? I read reviews. I talked to other yogis. And I decided to stick with what I already know I like and ordered another gaiam dry-grip. It's worked great in any type of class I've tried. Never had any issues with slipping. And I like the subtle design - not as boring as a plain colored mat, but not in your face either. I like that there's a little bit of extra weight to it - it stays in place on the studio floor and no worries about wind during outdoor classes. If I had to name a draw back, it would be that it is not reversible.

Original Review:
I have owned the black version of this mat for over a year and a half and it is still going strong. I'm so use to it that I have a hard time using the normal studio mats anymore on the rare occasion that I forget it. The mat still looks great and I still get people telling me that they like my mat and asking me what it is. I like that it has a design on it, but that it's subtle and not so in your face as a lot of mats. I take 3-4 yoga classes a week in addition to a home practice. This mat works great for flow, hot, aerial - basically any class I've used it in. I've even used it for some outdoor classes. I am not a heavy sweater, but in hot classes when I do work up a sweat, I've never had issues with slipping. The grip is great and the mat provides a good cushion over hard floors. Other mats I tried seemed squishy and the thickness just condensed down to nothing, but this mat is nice and dense and sturdy. To clean it, I just toss it in my bathtub and just use water to wipe it down super good and then let it air dry.

reviews.title: Sturdy bag, but too many practical problems
reviews.text:
NOTE: I received a free sample of this product for review.

I have a yoga mat bag that I like and use regularly ([[ASIN:B000VW4VWA Manduka MatSak Yoga Bag]]). However, it doesn't fit much other than my yoga mat, and I thought that something a bit roomier might be nice, especially given that I'm going to be starting yoga teacher training next month.

The YogaAddict Yoga Mat Bag is definitely very roomy! I liked that it has a U-type zippered opening. The main compartment is HUGE: I put my largest yoga mat inside, and there was plenty of room around it to add shoes, clothing, a water bottle, or whatever else I might want (other than the water bag, though, I don't usually take all of those things to yoga class). Also, the material of the bag felt very durable and sturdy.

Unfortunately, I couldn't find much else to like about this bag. I actually came to think of the large size as a detriment, as the stiff bag felt much too unwieldy to take to yoga class. In fact, the bag is SO large that I was actually able to fit TWO mats inside! This may sound like a good thing, but it just proves how unnecessarily massive this bag is. Furthermore, the material of the bag, while strong, also makes an extremely unpleasant crinkly sound: any time the bag is opened or any pocked it used, it sounds like a crumbling paper bag. Again, this seemed too disruptive for use during yoga class.

Other aspects of this bag seemed impractical as well. It has both double handles and a shoulder strap--at first glance, this seems like a good idea, but the double handles are shoulder length, so it is just cumbersome to include both, and they get in the way. There are three outside pockets, one apparently for a water bottle which has a non-functioning drawstring (it won't really tighten, at least not much), and two smallish zippered pockets that would have been much more functional had they been combined into one larger pocket. A final problem is a quality issue: there is also an inner zippered pocket, but on the bag I received, the pocket had been stitched into the lining of the bag, rendering it practically useless (see photos; pocket is sewn into seam in area of arrow).

In the end, there's just not a lot about this "Yoga Mat Bag" that makes sense to me. It even comes with a free "laundry bag" (a small drawstring bag made out of that same annoying, crinkly material)--but who uses a laundry bag for yoga? Perhaps this bag would function better as a general gym bag or some other type of sports bag, but it didn't work well for me.

reviews.title: Perfect for aerobics or for using under a step
reviews.text:
I was looking for a yoga mat that was thin enough to be stable under an aerobics step yet firm enough with enough give to use for shock absorption when dancing or running in place. I wasn't expecting miracles, but after reading many, many reviews, I decided to for for this one based on thinness, price, reviews of this mat and others and - what the heck - I liked the color. The one I ordered is the Turquoise Sea 4mm mat, and I paid full price for it out of my own pocket.

I was expecting to have to put the mat open in the garage for a few days, but when I pulled it out of the box and the plastic bag, it had no smell whatever. It is, indeed, quite thin - I prefer a thicker mat for poses on my knees or for doing situps on, but it's perfect for my needs. It keeps my aerobic step in place like it's glued to the floor, and it's actually really good at absorbing some of the impact when I walk or dance on it. Oh, and the color is exactly the same as it appeared on my monitor.

I expected to have to buy several mats before I found the right one, but I got lucky with this mat. I've bought a lot of things on Amazon that are okay, but for one reason or another, they are pretty meh. This mat isn't one of them. It is exactly what I wanted it to be with no smells and an attractive color. It is, indeed, sticky on the floor, and while it's too soon to see how durable it will be, it doesn't shed. And it's thin. It probably won't be enough padding if you want to spend long periods of time on your knees or doing 100 situps, but if you're actually looking for a thin mat, this 4mm one is definitely worth considering.

reviews.title: Firm Neck Pillow!
reviews.text:
I, personally, LOVE this pillow! I've tested it in many positions from stretching exercises to sleeping with it because I have suffered a very stiff neck for over 25 years.

Well, I've had it for quite a while now & for a stiff neck, this is what I found! I've been going through pillows like kleenex trying to find a pillow that won't kink my neck while I'm sleeping. Though, it took a bit of getting used to with the solidity of it & size, I have YET to wake up with neck pain since I began using it. Not Once! And that shocks me to no end, considering how solid & stiff this is made.

I also use it for back support when in bed watching my shows, on my side for legs when they cramp & for sleeping semi regularly. I've learned that between this & using no pillow, I no longer suffer stiff neck in the mornings or throughout the days, so for that alone, I give this 10 stars!

I've tried too many pillows to count that seem to work for a little bit, then that stiffness comes back on fire. I've tried so many cervical pillows that now are collected on the guest bed. Very frustrating since I deal with chronic pain.

I do wish it were a weeee softer, but being so firm, I believe that is the reason my neck doesn't hurt anymore so am not sure any softer would do my neck any good, but it DOES take getting used to if you are purchasing it for sleeping like I did.

Absolutely love this pillow!
Love the design! (I chose the design to go with the same designed mats)
Love the materials!
Love how well made it is!

When the time is right, will probably buy another few for decor as well as regular use!

reviews.text:
The mat is described as being 1.5mm thick and I guess I hadn't thought that through fully. It is very thin, but definitely better than working out on a dirty floor. Once in place on my tile floor, it does not move, so the non-slip feature works well. It looks nice and provides for a clean surface to work on. The description says it is lightweight, but I'm not sure that I'd describe it that way. It's almost 3 lbs, but it does rollup into a very small package (remember, there is almost no padding). Perhaps, by lightweight, they mean that it isn't very thick? I also don't understand their reference to 'suede' in the description -- it is rubber through and through. Maybe they meant to describe it as 'suede-like' because that could make some sense -- the surface is soft and sort-of suede-like.

The material feels quite rugged and I think it'll last a long time. Once unrolled flat, it stays, and when rolled up, it maintains that shape, too. It is so very non-slip that if it is rolled and the edges aren't aligned, there is no fixing it -- usually, if the edges aren't aligned, I could tap on the edge sticking out and it would even up, but this one just stays uneven. This is not at all a problem, but if you like your roll to be even, you'll have to be careful to align the edge with each roll.

reviews.title: Great for home practice but do not roll it up!
reviews.text:
I have recently rediscovered my love of yoga and I had been looking for the perfect mat to do anywhere from 3.5 hours to 10+ hours of practice per week.

After doing hours upon hours of research, I decided to try a BMAT out. First of all, it is incredibly comfortable. Sure, it attracts hair/fur and smells like all rubber mats, but it is easy to wipe off with a damp microfiber cloth and it in no way smells toxic. I mainly leave it out in my home office/gym room and ensure it is away from sunlight, but I tried rolling it up once for a few minutes while vacuuming and regret it. There are now creases on the bottom facing part of the mat, and I would have expected better for the price. Lesson learned - I now hang it over furniture and make sure there are no folds on the mat. Regardless, I would recommend it for home practice for those who want something out of rubber and don't expect 10 years out of a rubber mat (check out other big name brands, rubber mats just fall apart over time). I look forward to at least a year of yoga on this mat, 18 months if I am lucky! This mat would cost around 25 cents per day if it lasts a year - which I think is still a good value.

reviews.title: Good quality, attractive yoga mat
reviews.text:
This mat is sold specifically for yoga, but there are multiple possibilities for its use. It is also excellent for other types of exercise such as resistance-band exercises, Pilates, and various types of core work and stretching. It can be used as a camping mat, too.

I got this mat in the "blue shadow" shade. It is a lovely, light-green color. This mat is 68 inches long, which is a similar length to a regular mattress. Like most yoga mats, it has a soft, spongy, comfortable feel. It has a bumpy, sticky texture to prevent slipping. The instructions from the manufacturer are to wipe it down with a damp cloth just before using it to further increase the stickiness. It is also easy to keep this mat clean by wiping it down regularly with a damp, soft cloth.

I own four different brands of yoga mats, and several of the mats I own are of this same Gaiam brand. It's a bit more expensive than the generic brands sold at big-box, discount stores, but it seems to be worth the extra money. Especially since, as advertised, it does not seem to have as much of a toxic smell as most yoga mats do.

This is a 5 mm thick mat, and it might not be quite thick enough for some people. Yoga mats come in various thicknesses, however, so it is possible to get a thicker mat from this same Gaiam brand if desired. If you are working out on hard concrete or ceramic-tile flooring, a 5 mm mat like this one might not be enough padding. You might want a 10 mm mat instead.

reviews.title: Great thick yoga mat!
reviews.text: I live how thick and cushiony this yoga mat is! The mat can be dampened to increase the amount of traction that you have as well. As someone that uses this for advanced yoga classes, I find this to be a better mat compared to others I've had in the past that were paper thin, and offered little traction. The only thing I wished it came with was a mat holder for easy transport. Overall great quality.

reviews.title: Grippy and cushy
reviews.text:
This Gaiam mat is good for people with sweaty hands and feet like myself, or people who do hot yoga. I sweat so much due to medical issues I have to use yoga towels, yoga socks, and bear paw hand grips...so I was very interested in trying a mat that touts grippy benefits. It's no fun doing yoga when half of your focus is on not sliding off the mat.

This 5mm mat offers generous padding and doesn't slide around on the floor. It helps with grip when you get it, especially if you damped it slightly before using to activate what makes it kind of "tacky". It's not sticky or anything, it just helps.

It's also made with less controversial materials than other mats so if that's a concern this is a good option. It is free of DEHP, DBP, BBP, DINP, DIDP, and DNOP phthalates.

reviews.text:
This mat starts off with a terrible odor. Fortunately, it went away completely after a couple of days. It's the standard size, big enough for all the floor exercises that I do. It's also thick and comfortable, even for someone who weighs more than average. Nothing turns me off of working out more than pain in my elbows and knees from a thin yoga mat!

If you're lying down or sitting, the mat is fantastic. If you're doing any standing exercises or moves that dig your toes into the mat (like planking), you may want to take your shoes off to avoid wearing out the foam. It has, however, survived my two German Shepherd dogs running all over it to "help" me exercise.

For the price, it's a good deal. I'm tempted to get more than one. The ocean blue is beautiful. My next one will be seafoam with the lovely pattern.

We got this in our house yesterday, just in time for our weekly sessions with our trainer. Right up front, its superior thickness enabled us to replace two thin, cheapo mats, and provided greater comfort in use. reviews.title: Great mat, very impressed with it.
reviews.text:
This seems like an excellent, well made yoga mat. Having only used it a few times it's a little tough give firm opinions on it as some of the things could go either way over the long haul. However, I like it a lot and it's currently my main mat. Here's what I've found so far:

Pros:
Better than average grip, almost too good. It can be hard to make slight adjustments, requiring you to pick up your hand/foot instead of just slide it slightly. A little annoying for transitions like Warrior 1 to Warrior 2. However, overall it's a good feature. It's still slippery when wet. So in a hot class the grip might last a little longer, but as soon as there's significant sweat, you're going to need a towel.

Good materials and construction. The bottom has a different texture than the top. They say you can use either side, but it seems like the lighter side texture is better for gripping the floor. So far I've only used it with the darker side facing up.

The mat is very thick and feels like felt. Personally, I like mats on the thicker side so I think it's great. The 'felt' feel to it worries me a little bit since it seems like it'll absorb sweat and require more cleaning than usual. So far no problem, but we'll see.

It's a bit too thick/soft to use on carpet. It's great on a hardwood floor, so when I'm in a studio it's fine. However, I occasionally practice at my house and it has carpet. A thinner mat works better for that. Not really a complaint, just a fyi, the ProSource mat is clearly designed for use on a hard floor and it works great there.

Long: 72" A requirement for me since I'm 6 feet tall.

Cons:

I'm getting used to the extra grip. As mentioned, it makes slight adjustments a bit more difficult.

It feels kind of plush. I like thick mats, so it's great, but it may not be for everyone.

The claim of TPE being 'environmentally friendly' is a bit of stretch. It's better than PVC but there seems to be mixed information about how eco-friendly it is. And trying to find a place to recycle a TPE mat is difficult. you can't just put it in the recycle bin. Something to consider if you _really_ want a eco-mat.

reviews.title: I'm so disappointed...
reviews.text:
I really really wanted to like this. There were tons of rave reviews all over the internet for this mat. In particular, countless mentions of how unbelievably sticky it is. Basically endless claims of how it's the stickiest mat they've ever felt.

I hardly ever sweat at all on my body. I am not a sweaty person. However, my hands and feet? They can get pretty wet. That being said, it's incredibly important for me to use a sticky mat to maintain Downdog and other asanas.

When I first excitedly ripped open the packaging on this mat, I was immediately smacked in the face with this incredibly strong odor.
"What IS that?!" I exclaimed.
"It smells like...fish." my mom replied while wrinkling her nose.

AND IT DOES. IT REEKED OF FISH. Those complaints about the Jade Harmony mat and the Lululemon mats smelling bad? They ain't got nothin' on this Eau de Fish. Luckily, after unrolling it on the floor and leaving it to air out overnight, the odor dissipated. So I was able to take the mat to class without smelling like a seafood market.

The surface of this mat is quite smooth, unlike the rough texture of the Jade Harmony. Though not as smooth as the smooth side of a Lululemon mat. When your hands are dry, without a doubt, the grip on this Bmat is quite good. My mother said it was much too grippy for her tastes.

I took my Bmat to an easygoing Hatha yoga class this morning and lemme tell ya. It was like a SLIP 'N SlIDE. As soon as my hands had a hint of sweat on them, they started slipping. The worst part was, when my feet started sweating as well, the sweat began to literally pool on top of the smooth mat into little mini puddles. I'm not even the type of person that drips sweat. It was purely sweat from my hands and feet. And because of the smooth surface, there was no place for the water to go. It just sat there.
I could barely even hold an asana as upright as a Warrior 2 because of how dang slippery this mat was.

Even my mom's $10 generic yoga mat that I've been using for the past few weeks felt better than this $85 (including tax) designer mat. The generic yoga mat has that rounded bumps texture that I could at least hold on to if I was sweaty. Because the Bmat is smooth, when I was sweaty, I had absolutely nothing to grip on to so I was constantly slipping.
I spent the whole class feeling so unstable I couldn't enjoy my hour of yoga practice whatsoever.

Pros:
- Made in Spain
- Pretty color
- Seems like a good company

Cons:
- Out of the box has a strong fishy smell
- Pools sweat
- Super slippery with even a hint of wetness

Even when dry, this mat is not as grippy as a Lululemon mat. I know a lot of people crap on that mat (maybe because they think the company is so overrated?) but I really think it's quite good. I loved the Jade Harmony's stickiness as well (it even ripped a couple of my hairs out on occasion), but the smell was pretty overwhelming and never really went away. It's also super heavy.

Anyway, I'm really sorry this mat didn't work out for me. I was really looking forward for this to be a winner after all the good reviews. But like all things, your mileage may vary and you don't know until you try it yourself. Back to Amazon it goes!

* Reasonable-sized pocket separate from bladder.

reviews.title: Great Priced Sleeping Pad
reviews.text:
This sleeping pad is worth the money. I can't attest to its R value since I've only used indoors (I live in Colorado and winter makes it hard to camp) but the comfort is equal to sleeping pads I have which cost 5x the price of this one. I spent 2 nights on it indoors and I tend to toss and turn during the night. This one is comfortable for side sleepers, and those who sleep on their backs or stomachs. Mine never lost air during the night, and I woke rested like I slept in a bed.

Mine came with 6 repair patches in case it gets a hole punctured in it. I love this because lots of Colorado camping means sleeping on ground that has an inevitable sharp object.

The design is flexible too, so it'll adapt to the ground you're sleeping on. No campsite is ever flat.

It took me roughly 30 breaths to fill mine up without the inflatable sack, and probably about as much time as using the inflatable sack. I didn't try it with an electric pump because I never bring one camping. It's easy enough to deflate and pack into the included stuff sack.

Great product and great value.

reviews.title: Instruction sheet needs work
reviews.text:
I was very excited to find a camping pad that I didn’t have to blow up or use a pump. So I was surprised to see on the instruction sheet that the first 2 methods listed for inflation were (1) “blow air directly with mouth” and (2) “manual or electric air pump”! That being said, there is a third option - using the supplied “air bag”. But the directions for using it are inadequate. Luckily, my husband and I figured it out:
A. Attach the air valve on the air bag to the mattress air valve.
B. Open the bag fully, then clasp the top together (capturing the air inside) and continue to roll it closed, pushing the captured air into the mattress (as shown in the photo on the instruction sheet).
C. When all the air is moved into the mattress, simply unroll the bag and repeat - you don’t even need to detach the bag from from the mattress to refill the air bag.
It takes about 4 bags to fill the mattress - and it is pretty easy once you get the hang of it. Very clever.
The mattress material is a little thinner than I expected, so we will see how it lasts when camping (concerned will become punctured when using it outside). Also, the quilted design does not give a good barrier from the cold ground.
All that being said, it is very lightweight for carrying with a nice carrying sack. The comfort is medium (definitely better than sleeping on the ground but not super cushy). The length can accommodate taller folk - I am 5’8” and had nearly another foot in length.

reviews.title: Lightweight and portable, unusual design
reviews.text:
A step up from the thin pad I've used in previous camping trips! This is a good design for a camping sleeping pad perfect for car camping, and probably good for backpacking as well.

Wins:
- Easy to inflate with a machine (NOT included), took less than 30 seconds for me. Manually (blowing) probably would take a few minutes. One-way valve at least ensures that air won't leak out during filling
- When lying on my back, good cushioning and will hold up on most flat surfaces
- Lightweight and compact - with included carrying sack, dimensions come to about 8 inches x 4 x 4 to easy to stick in a pack or duffel

Challenges:
- The design is a series of mini pockets in a cross/diagonal pattern with no air in between. As a result, putting too much weight in any one area (e.g. sitting up, or side sleeping) results in hitting the ground. Best for back (or stomach) sleepers and would not recommend for sitting
- Filling bag/pillow? doesn't really work. Unfortunately no instructions included so maybe I was doing something wrong but the claim that 3 bags will fill the mat just doesn't seem right. I think (?) the air bag is meant to double as a pillow...I tried a few times but it only stayed inflated for a couple minutes before the air leaked out. Odd design.

reviews.title: Easy to Inflate, Comfortable, and Lightweight
reviews.text: I like how easy it was to inflate this sleeping pad. Just 10 to 12 times using the included manual inflation bag and voila! You got yourself a nice comfy sleeping pad in under 2 minutes. The sleeping pad I ordered is in the olive drab color which I prefer, and the stuff sack and manual inflation bag that came with the sleeping pad are also in olive drab color. The sleeping pad is long enough for me--I'm 5'7" and I had plenty of room that my feet were nowhere near the bottom edge of the sleeping pad, where I reckon I had about a foot or so of space there before my feet reach the edge. The sleeping pad is comfortable and long enough, but I wish it was a bit wider, since I cannot lay down on it with both arms on my side without either arm falling off the sleeping pad and onto the ground/pavement/floor. Also, I would not recommend placing this sleeping pad directly onto rough ground, since the bottom of the pad is not reinforced with anything, so do use something to put on the ground before laying the sleeping pad on it. Still, it is a pretty decent piece of kit, and at this price point, it is a decent deal. If you are in the market for an entry-level sleeping pad, then why not give this one a quick look-see? It's one of the better entry-level sleeping pads at this price point.

reviews.title: Colorful coverage
reviews.text:
My family and I recently went on a 7 day backpacking adventure here in the NW. Even in August, you can experience rain in the mountains, and indeed we did. We had decided to forego our rain jackets and backpack rain covers for the poncho, in an attempt to save some precious weight, and we were glad we did. It was warm and raining, so the poncho provided coverage, but air circulation underneath, keeping us cooler than our rain jackets (I like the option of looping the poncho underneath you or not). When the rain subsided, we could still use the poncho over our packs to keep the packs dry while making our way through all the saturated underbrush.

Our packs were large, and the ponchos fit well, with ample room to spare (although we are all smaller framed folk). We also liked the option of being able to use the ponchos as temporary tarps for food preparation or storage.

All three of us chose different colors, so we were easily identifiable to each other on the trail when we became separated.

reviews.title: Well designed simple backpacking poncho, but not waterproof enough
reviews.text:
I'm very impressed by the thoughtful design of this backpacking poncho. It is one-size-fits-all, and is big on me (5'7") and also big on my husband (6'), but not in a bad way. This will be easy to put on while on the trail over any amount of clothes. The sleeves seem a little short, but are loose enough that I can easily pull my arms inside and stay entirely covered, and their slightly shorter length means I'll be able to use my hands without the sleeves getting in the way.
Despite being big, it has toggles and cinches to "fit" it to the wearer and hold it in place. It has capacity to cover a huge backpack, but zips down smaller for use over a smaller backpack or no pack.
The hood is very large, but also cinches down to fit the wearer's head. It has a stiff bill to keep water out, but is soft enough to pack easily. Another reviewer mentioned how loud the hood is, but it's no noisier than any other unlined rain hood.
The quality of the poncho is what you expect for the price.
Total weight with stuff sack is 12 oz.

I haven't yet tested this in rough conditions, so I plan to update and hope my rating doesn't change.

UPDATE: this was pretty much a total failure on a day-long hike in heavy rain and stormy winds. Rain soaked through the poncho and completely wetted every item in the bag, right down to the bills in my wallet deep in the pack. I also fought with the poncho all day in the wind even with everything clipped and cinched down. A raincoat and rainpants were much more effective and less annoying in similar conditions the following day, but also much hotter. I would limit using this (if possible) to light rain and non-windy conditions, and for backpacking, I would probably always choose good quality rain gear over this all in one.

this tents real time water proofness was untested until an unexpected storm pounded me and my companions on a long excursion in the desert. This tent DID hold up to the downpour. It kept me and my friend who was "rooming" with me dry while everyone else's tent leaked a little on them. We had to set up in a rush, and never having put it together before, in the wind and starting of sprinkle, it took about 5-7 minutes I think. The one pole design greatly simplifies and speeds things along. It fit both of us well, with about half our gear on the inside, and half on the out under the flaps. (it did get damp and VERY muddy, but not soaked.) with room left for us to play cards on the floor of the tent. To take down it took us about 15-20 minutes the first time. WORD TO THE WISE: Pay careful attention to the factory folds when you first set it up. the tent and rain fly are oddly shaped; If you do not pay attention to how it was folded when it cam from the factory, how to successfully fold and re-pack this tent will plague you as long as you own it. I've had it now 3 years and because I did not do this I STILL haven't figured out how I'm suppose to fold the thing and each time i try it a different way resulting in verifying levels of success and sizes when put back it the storage sack. PLEASE DO YOUR SELF A FAVOR and heed this advise! Although the shape is a pain to fold and put back (especially in the high wind as was my first experience) the innovative shape has good wind and water resistance when set up, and even snow resistance. I got caught in a snow storm on an extensive road trip recently and had to set up in the dark in the snow. I was half buried in the morning but the tent held up and the trees above me plopped moderately weighted snow loads from there limbs on the top of the tent and for the most part the snow slid off. I put the tent down on a hastily thrown down tarp on top of dead brush of some sort and snow and ice. light Moister did accumulate on the floor of the tent under my sleeping bag that night and I have noticed it a time or 2 since. if you like to have to have a hot drink, like me, in the evening in your tent by means of boiling water on a backpacking stove or some such, or making breakfast in the morning, keep in mind the water vaper/steam will not vent out easily. the moister will accumulate on the ceiling in most cases and the steam will stay with you for a long time. WORD TO THE WISE: if you can don't boil in your tent but under the little door flap, or as I call it... on my deck :D. doing this you will still be protected by the weather for the most part and it will minimize the water vaper problem, but if you cant do that for whatever reason the bit of vaper honestly wont be a HUGE issue unless your boiling A LOT or water. One flaw is that you can not use the rainfly, which is a crucial part of the tent system, with out the stakes. and i couldn't pound even the steel stakes I bought to supplement the provided aluminum ones that have tendency to bend when going trough harder ground, through the ice, so I had to resort to tying the rainfly to the bushes and trees that were around with my frozen hands. I feel that is the one true flaw with this system, but its only once or twice its effected me greatly and I was always able to improvise something. I was alone that time and could keep all the gear I needed in my tent with me. However, On a different occasion, in the summer, Despite the tent's 1-2 people advertisement, I DID fit up to 3 people in this tent, and you could too. I'm 5'6" on a good day, those with me were 5'7" & 5'8", we were touching shoulder to shoulder on our backs the whole time, and it was quite warm (summer) and almost no gear was inside, but in a pinch it can be done and unless you have a complainer in the group it'll all be good, maybe even a fun story/experience to tell!

PROs-
- it IS actually water proof.
-innovative shape is wind water snow resistant
-single pole design makes for fast and simple set up (3-5 min when you get good)
-Weight/size as advertised
-extra outdoor storage space
-1-2 person tent can fit 3 in a pinch
-Quality storage bag
-Price point, your getting a better product then your paying for.
CONs-
-Rain fly requires being staked
-innovative shape is a pain to fold up and put away (7-10 min ideal conditions)
-ventilation quality debatable
-nothing that allows you to hang a light from the top of the ceiling
-floor condensation issue MAY exist to a very limited extent... Limited date on this so don't quote me.

I would be happy to recommend this tent to anyone who is on a budget or who's got money to burn. I don't foresee this tent failing anytime soon, but if I did need to replace it ill probably get another one of the same. I am very happy with this product.

In case you don't know, a percolator is the best pot to use for cooking whole asparagus spears. Drop a bunch of @ 6" stalks tip-up into a pot containing enough boiling water to almost cover them. After @ 4 minutes (thickness-dependent) the tougher bottom of the stalks will soften in the hotter bottom of the pot while the tender tips steam above the bubbling upper water.

You can also make coffee in a percolator, though purists don't recommend it. I have in-laws who prefer percolated, but I find it makes strong, acidic coffee. The percolator apparatus is light aluminum, but I guess that's par for the course.

Twenty bucks seems like a lot for this item, which is pretty basic - as someone else says, the clasp holding the lid to the top of the kettle is a cheap stamping, but it would be as easy to bend back into shape as to bend it out of shape, so I guess it's... a VERY flexible item? ;- Anyway, I'd rather have my money going to Mexico than China!

reviews.title: Have Used For Years - Very Good For Fire Starting
reviews.text: I have used WetFire tinder for many years as a means to start a fire in the woods, or at home.  It's easy to shave a little bit amongst other tinder, and get more material going.  With any kind of spark or ember, I can get a flame more consistently with WetFire shavings than from any other commonly carried tinder (charred cloth, cotton balls with Vaseline in candle wax, birch bark, magnesium shavings, tinder fungus or dryer lint).  I can often get a flame from a single strike of a flint.  There have been a few exceptions, but never more than three strikes.  The variance seems to be from tab to tab.  I'll have one tab, from which shavings always light on the first strike.  I'll have another tab, from which shavings always take two or three strikes.  I'll get these inconsistencies from new batches, and old batches.  Age doesn't seem to be the issue, as I've had the same variances from brand new packs and 2-year old packs.  Out of a pack of eight tabs, there's always one - rarely two - that doesn't catch alight as fast as the others.  Still, that's far more dependable than other tinder types.  That said, I never go without AT LEAST TWO - often three - different types of tinder (in an emergency "one is zero, two is one, three is two, etc.").  I've been quite pleased with WetFire tinder for many years, and I'll continue to use it as my first tinder source - but I'll always have a backup.

reviews.title: Basic information on oil lanterns
reviews.text:
This is just an overview on oil lanterns. I wish I had the time to write this on every oil lantern review. #1 paraffin is wax, paraffin lantern oil has paraffin wax in it, the wax WILL clog lantern/lamp wicks and it will burn poorly in lanters. The only thing paraffin oil is good for are large round wicks like a tiki torch.
#2 even the highest quality oil lantern will leak if there filled to full. As the oil heats up in the tank, the oil expands and overflows if to full, making it look like it leak's. If you unsure how much fuel to use don't fill it much more than half full.

reviews.title: Bail handle fell off on first use
reviews.text:
I tried it over an alcohol stove. The stove is enthusiastic and flames lick up the side of the pot, and since the bail wire handle doesn't have an upright locking position, that means the flame directly heats the handle. It expanded and fell off the pot. I can imagine how that would have gone if I'd been using it to support the pot.

Basically, bad design. Whatever metal they used for the handle, it shouldn't have been one that expanded when heated. I will probably use pliers to bend things so it doesn't happen again, but this is fundamentally an unsafe design and it should be tested before you rely on it.

reviews.text: I'm a minimalist, I count my weight in ozs, and have been backpacking for 24 years. Gear has changed a lot through the years, and I've been through my share of packs. For a an average 6 day trip my pack will weigh between 17-25 lbs depending on the season. This includes my shelter, sleep system, cooking, fuel, food, 4lbs of water and everything I need to survive. This isn't my lightest pack. What caught my attention were the load lifters, which really do help duffle bag style packs ride a little better. Overall I was satisfied with this pack. It had a ton of room, I didn't use a pack cover I use compactor bags and atuff sacks to keep my gear dry. So far no leaks no problems. I'm not gentle with my gear and so far despite putting hundreds of miles on this pack no issues. I wish the mesh pouch on the front was a tad bigger I leave my 19 oz tarp tent and 2 oz ground cover in it to dry along with a few things however it does take some working packing them in to the mesh. The side pockets are deep and snug. I don't like that there aren't any hip belt pockets. I bought some cubein fiber ones from zpaks which fit okay...  I don't like the way the belt is attached to the buckle I have a lot of extra material dangling from both sides. Other than those few gripes the pack has performed well, and has been comfortable. I felt like I got a good deal with the price being so low.

Time will tell how it holds up, but so far it looks like it should be a relatively durable bag. There is not a ton of padding in the straps, but it is intended to be a lightweight bag. The included rain cover in the bottom of the pack is a nice addition. The blue fabric is a good color and the pack overall looks pretty modern and trendy. Kailas is a brand worth keeping an eye on, it seems like some of their other offerings are fairly solid as well. Decent quality pack and overall decent buy, especially if you don't have a nearby outdoor store to try stuff locally.

reviews.title: Very Comfortable Backpack!
reviews.text: This is my favorite backpack for hiking! It fits really well, and it has an amazing number of expandable pockets also.  I like the space suspension feature for your back. This will keep the backpack cool while hiking in hot weather. One surprise I wasn’t expecting was the rain cover that you can find in the bottom zippered compartment. Now your backpack can be protected rain or shine. It is a little heavier than I expected. But not so much that it would be too heavy with my using it on hikes through the preserves here in Southwest Florida.  It has loads of room in the inner compartment. The padded shoulder straps adjust perfectly for me, I’m 5’9”, and it feels very comfortable.  I highly recommend this backpack.

reviews.title: Little pricey, but pretty good pack
reviews.text:
I picked up this bag awhile back and I am generally pleased with it. The 28L capacity is suitable for a weekend camping trip, and the included rain cover is a useful feature for unexpected weather. The backpack seems well-constructed with solid zippers and comfortable straps.

The only minor issue I have is with the price, which I think is a bit steep at $70. However, the backpack's quality and added features do justify the cost to some extent.

Overall, I would rate this backpack 3.5 out of 5 stars. I would recommend it to someone looking for a spacious and dependable camping backpack, but be aware of the slightly higher price tag.

reviews.title: Total Osprey dupe!
reviews.text: This hiking pack is amazing! The quality is top-notch. If you are familiar with Osprey backpacks, this feels like a total dupe. The features, design, materials, quality, zippers, and accessories all feel identical to a hiking pack priced at least $100 more at REI. The outlet for a hydration pack hose was a little tricky to find, but it's just the half-moon slit at the top right where it makes sense for it to be.  I seriously can't enough wonderful things, it's just SO nice. This would make a fantastic gift for anyone that hikes.

reviews.title: Ok, but not fantastic.
reviews.text: I bought these to try them.  I tried all three varieties.  They were all decent, and I don't regret my purchase, but they also weren't exceptional.  These are fully hydrated meals, so they aren't quite as light as a freeze dried meal.  All three meals had a strong flavor profile, which is nice, as bland food isn't very appealing.

reviews.title: Would be good as an emergency food or for camping
reviews.text:
These ready-made meals would be a convenient item to bring camping, and would be easy to fix in a pot of water heated on a fire. I did not try them cold, nor are they recommended as a cold item, so you would need to have at least a pot for water to heat them, and the packages are fairly heavy (as mentioned by another reviewer) so they would not be a light item to take hiking. So, these would likely be best if you were not trying to pack light. One bonus is that the bag is very easy to rip open, so you would not need to have scissors or any other way to open the package. And the bags fit together nicely so would not take up excessive room, and can be tucked around other items.

As an emergency item, they have a good shelf life (2 years) and do not take up too much room, so would be a good item to have on hand in case of emergency.

I tried the beef ragu and beef stew, and shared them with my family. I heated them in the microwave fo 2 minutes which got them quite hot. The instructions say 3 minutes, but it also says that is for an 800W microwave, and mine is more powerful than that. Here are our impressions of the two flavors.

Beef Stew --
-The overall flavor is good
-The beef is a little tough -- I had to chew the pieces a bit, but the flavor was good.
-The vegetables were soft
-The broth was fairly thin. I have a picture both before and after cooking, and you can see how much thinner the beef stew is compared to the beef ragu (picture before cooking).
- The beef stew has lower calories, lower sugar, lower sodium, slightly higher fiber, and about the same protein as the beef ragu. I would think it is likely the healthier option of the two. It is also gluten-free, which the ragu is not.
Everybody in my family also preferred the beef stew to the beef ragu.

Beef Ragu -
- The consistency is thicker than the stew, but the pasta was a little mushy
- The beef is in fairly small pieces.
- The texture was a little strange. My aunt described it as gritty. It made it slightly less appealing.
- The overall flavor was good.

Overall, while I would not likely choose to eat this for a typical lunch, these pre-packaged foods would be a very good option for their marketed purpose of either being a camping food or emergency food. They would provide good nutrients quickly and easily.

The price point is a bit high, so if money is a concern, these might not be the best option, but they are a convenient healthy option for camping or emergencies.

reviews.title: Great tasting camping food
reviews.text: These packets are already made. All you have to do is heat them up. They are compact and tasty. High protein quantity and kept me full for quite a while. The beef ragu is tasty and is like a chili mac. The stew is hearty and not big chunks of meat, but definitely enough to keep you full. Similar to the US MRE type meals only I would say these are a bit tastier. You don't need to add salt or hot sauce for a decent flavor.

reviews.title: Very good for what they are
reviews.text:
I'm going to start out by being very blunt: these are not for backpacking. They weigh a lot because they are fully hydrated, heat and eat products. they would be excellent if you are car camping or if you have a short hike, but the weight-to-calorie ratio isn't good enough, in my opinion.

Personally, I thought they tasted great. I had both of them earlier today, and I really enjoyed the beef ragu, and I thought the beef stew was pretty good, too. The beef stew has nice chunks of meat in it, and the beef ragu has a wonderful sauce. This is better than Chef Boyardee, that's for sure, and boy are they packed with protein.

That's pretty much where my praise has to end. At $8 per meal, it's hard to recommend them. Yes, they're good, but their impracticality as a backpacking food outweighs how good they taste. Plus, I ate one of each and don't think only one would be filling at all, especially if you've been hiking for hours. As I mentioned before, I would totally bring these car camping and fully intend to. Or, you could just leave a few of them in your car in case of emergency.

I really struggled between giving these a three or four-star review. Ultimately I went with a 4 because I really do think they're tasty and convenient. While I think they are a little bit expensive, I have seen camping meals that cost way more. Those ones tend to be lighter, mind you, but it is what it is.

I liked these a lot, and if you're okay with the price, you may, too.

features: GREAT FOR ALL PLAYERS- The Dynamic Discs Paratrooper disc golf bag is the bigger brother to the popular Trooper bag. It features more structure, padding, durability, and storage.

reviews.title: Superb Value Disc Bag
reviews.text:
I bought this for 60 bucks. At that price point you are getting an insanely good value. I upgraded from DD Trooper which is similar and did an admirable job for a couple of years but did finally start to wear out. I was going to spend a bit more ($100 range) for an upgraded bag, but after seeing this one I realized that I could get all the features I wanted for less. Now I do have friends that have more expensive bags from US manufacturers and I won't knock them at all. They seem very happy with those bags but the cost ramps up into the $300 + range, which was simply more than I was willing to spend.

So what you get in the paratrooper is a sturdy and functional bag. The main pouch can easily hold up to 20 discs. I probably would suggest holding a couple less in there as if you use the putter pouch it restricts the ease of access to the main pouch. By leaving a little room in there you can more easily insert and remove discs you use. The paratrooper comes with two compartments above the main opening, and I use them both. One I use for putters and the other I use for my go to mid range and second most used driver. Then on the flap for the main pouch I use my go to driver. So I have 6 discs that are very easily accessible, which is awesome because those are truly the ones I use the most.

For the side pouches, they are large and plenty big to store whatever I need on the course. I have sunblock, bug spray, extra towel, sharpie and I keep my phone, keys and wallet in my bag while I play. They also have an interior pocked for sliding in your phone or wallet. Very nice. I like having two water bottle holders. One I use with a 40 oz bottle and it easily fits. The other I tuck in a towel and grip sack. This allows me to keep those things dry on damp days. On hotter days or multi-round days, I would imagine I would bring 2 water bottles unless I knew of a place to refill my 40 oz bottle.

The bag comes with 4 plastic inserts (1 for each side) to keep the bag stable. I think you can decide whether or not to use them. I tried them with and without and have decided that I prefer the extra stability that they offer. It is slightly softer and probably more comfortable bag to carry with them out, but I would frankly rather have the bag be more rigid. I noticed that the bag tended to fall over more without the inserts. The one insert I decided to leave out was the front one, as I wanted the front of the bag to be more pliable for easy disc removal. The zippers are elastic bands which are nice as they are easy to grab and you can clip things through the loops.

Cons. No bag is perfect so the small nit picky things I would point out is that it would be nice to have a couple of d-rings at the top of the bag as the trooper had to clip on things like towels or dry sacks. But as noted before there are other places to stick those things. Also you can buy a small carabiner and attach it to the zipper for the top putter pouch. The top easy access pouch is a little big and when used can interfere a bit with the accessibility of discs in the main pouch. I took a couple of safety pins to make the very top pouch slightly less deep and the second pouch I used the velcro to pin it to the back of the bag.

In sum, you get a ton of features for the price paid. I have seen plenty of bags at twice the price with similar or less features. I can't fully speak to the durability, as I have only used it for a couple of weeks, but my impression is that it is well made and I expect it to last several years. I highly recommend this bag. I don't think you will be disappointed if you give it a try.
