reviews.title: Way better than I was expecting...
reviews.text: I have to be honest and admit I didn't have high hopes for this stove. I have been using Snow Peak and MSR stove until this one and I can say that this stove is as good as those from my first impressions. Build quality and "heft" of premium materials are both present and the actual operation is on par as well with a steady 3:45 boil. Would definitely buy again.

reviews.title: A great stove, not for smaller pots.
reviews.text:
This is a good stove.
It is regulated, which means that it runs at a consistent gas pressure regardless of the ambient temperature, (within reason of course).
This is nice, as standard isobutane usually becomes unusable at lower temperatures due to butane gas liquifieing around freezing temps, (32-F or 0-C). This means that as you approach freezing, the cannisters provide less pressure, thus less flame/heat from the stove.
A regulated stove helps with that to a degree and offers a bit greater ability at low temps.
Once you get down below freezing though, no amount of regulation is going to help...
The construction of the stove is excellent. Stainless steel arms fold out securely and are very stable.
The concave construction of the burner helps mitigate wind, making the stove more efficient in a light breeze. However, you will still need a windscreen or some kind of wind break, (rock, log, sit pad, etc) in a stiffer breeze.
The weight is a reasonable 2.7oz, (~76g), which is right in line with other stoves with these features.
The included carrying case is very high quality. It does add another ounce or so and a bit of bulk. A lightweight backpacker will probably opt to just leave it at home as the stove is robust enough to really not need it. Just wrap it in a bandanna and shove it in your pack.
There is no piezoelectric ignition feature. Honestly, I've never been a huge proponent of those anyway as every one I've ever used has eventually failed, and they add a bit of weight and bulk to the stove. Bring a mini-bic. Keep it in your cook set and that's all the lighter you'll ever need.
The only complaint I have about this stove is that the pot supports are just a bit too wide to safely hold my 750ml titanium cook pot. It'll fit on there...just barely though, and the slightest bump or jiggle could potentially cause boiling hot water or food to spill. See attached photos.
If you use a wider pot, then I think this would be an excellent stove choice for backpacking.
Similar stoves can be $20-30 more. There are some excellent options out there from major manufacturers. I think this stove competes with them very well and provides an excellent value.
Highly recommended...if you use a wider pot...

reviews.title: Great stove for the money
reviews.text: It is comparable in every aspect to the best stoves in the category. Especially price. If it goes up in price, it will cease to be a bargain, but at less than $40, it gives you the features you want for less. It is light, especially if you ditch the carry case. It provides regulated flame. It has a concave burner so it resists breezes a bit better. It connects easily and doesn't leak. The sets up easy and supports my cookpot just fine. Other reviewers said it was a bit too large for some vessels, but my kit fit fine. Overall, a great value for money.

reviews.title: Lacking a Piezo - but impressive beyond that
reviews.text: Gear is my sickness. I have similar stoves that are lighter (titanium) and self-igniting (Piezo) in the same general price range. Not having a piezo is the Achilles' Heel of this particular stove. But it stands out for its higher altitude/colder weather performance capabilities due to regulator and hose design. Case is good, materials seem quality, build seems sturdy...overall a very worthy backcountry option for minimalists. However - when it comes to a versatile, all-in-one cooking solution for backcountry I go with Jetboil. No fuss, no muss, no cleanup - water boils, goes into freeze-dried food bag, mix w/ spork, let it sit, eat, dispose of bag, lick spork clean, end of meal. With a stove like this, you need a pot or a pan. Personal choice I suppose....

reviews.title: Powerful and light!
reviews.text:
A very powerful stove that's lightweight and easily packs down.
The remote regulator is a great addition allowing you to move the fuel canister to get the best flow in differnt altitudes and climates.
The stove puts out heat and fast, about 3 to 4 minutes to get a rolling boil. The only complaint if it is one is that when using it on high it does get fairly loud, kind of like how a wok burner or a blow torch sounds, but for the speed it heats up in, it's a solid compromise for me.
Didn't have any luck trying fuels other than Isobutane but that was to be expected, and I had to try!
All in all, this is a great backpack stove!

reviews.title: Nice little pad
reviews.text:
I’ve been backpacking for decades and I’ve carried and slept on lots of different pads. This pad has some nice features. I like the idea that several pads have now with a built in inflation pump. This one works fine and inflated in just a couple of minutes. When the pad is inflated, the pillow end is nice and supportive and the main pad is comfy. It is a good size for a full size sleeping bag and is wide enough that my arms stay on the pad easily. This pad is a little thinner than some I’ve used, and I was a little worried about how supportive it would be when I lay on my side. It was no problem. The pillow was thick enough to support my head on the side and I still did not feel the ground through the pad. Taking down the pad was simple and quick. The included bag was large enough to fit the pad easily
I weighed the pad and bag. It came to 1 pound 5 ounces. Not the very lightest, but for its size and the built in pump, not bad at all. It was only 2.5 ounces more than my wife’s Klymit pad and hers is hard to repack and has no pump. If I have any reservation about this pad it is that it will not give a lot of insulation between you and the ground. In the spring, summer and fall that won’t be much of a problem, but I wouldn’t recommend it for cold camping.
Altogether, a nice light pad.

reviews.title: Very cool portable sleeping mat!
reviews.text: This is a pretty great inflatable mat. At first I was frustrated because the instructional card it came with was not totally clear on the manual inflation technique. However, I opened up the listing on Amazon and it was easier to understand. Basically, you keep the gray latch closed, the red one open and to inflate, you actually put your hand over the red hole and push down (kind of like one handed cpr compressions. I was skeptical but it really did inflate in about a minute! It says your can use your foot too but I found it easier with my hands. Anyway, I found this pretty comfortable laying down - as my husband said- "it's definitely better than sleeping on the ground" , and or rolls up neatly in a small pouch. I can see this having many uses!

reviews.title: A Good Sleeping Pad Option
reviews.text:
[[VIDEOID:905db8d3ef694ef76c8e048d1ad0cec6]] This sleeping pad is a good option. Why just "good"? I'll start with on the plus side:
- Relatively light weight @ 1 lb.
- Full length with integrated pillow
- Inflates relatively fast (This is helped by it being "quilted" vs inflating the entire area of the pad)
- Anti-backflow valve so you don't lose air when you remove your mouth during inflation

Some places where it could have done better:
- The valve "whistles" when you blow into it (I plan to ask the manufacturer about this)
- The inflation aid is not much help, but might provide help to fine tune firmness; you will still have to inflate it by mouth or pump
- The instructions are lacking

This is still a good pad. Assuming the "whistling" valve is a manufacturing issue, I would recommend it.

reviews.title: Looks good! Will update soon!
reviews.text:
So far so good! I haven’t been able to test it yet, but here a few thoughts so far. I was going to return it because I ended up with multiple paddleboards after Amazon Prime Day, but I’m hanging on to it. My husband used the Shop-Vac to inflate it mostly in our living room, then we both took turns with the manual pump. The pump says “new” on it, so maybe it’s an improved version. The pump worked fine. It’s important to realize that the psi won’t even register until about 5 psi and even then it takes a while for the needle to move. On the bottom of the paddleboard, it says that the recommended psi is 12 and that’s what we are planning on for all of our paddleboards. 15psi is the maximum. I would not recommend that you try using any sort of inflation option without leaving the last amount of inflation to the manual pump. No doubt it’s hard work and more difficult for a shorter person with a “belly”. It’s best to have two people sharing the hard work! One observation is that there are NO d-rings to attach a seat. That’s a drawback and something the company might want to address for future improvement. Many paddleboards have d-rings for a seat. Four are needed towards the middle of the board. The other observation is that the green version has a lot of white on it, so it could get dirty-looking over time depending on where you paddle. Other than that, it looks good so far! The foam top looks good and the inflation valve worked perfectly. On the manual pump there are two openings at the top. You need to connect the hose to the one that says “out”. I learned this much! The bag seems fine and I’ll check out the paddle and update my review.
Happy Paddling!

reviews.title: IN DEPTH Review Of This Backpack
reviews.text:
WARNING- This is an IN DEPTH review of this backpack to help those who are trying to make serious buying decisions. If you prefer a more brief summary, please see section marked THE BOTTOM LINE
----------------------------
When it comes to summer time and even Spring or Fall, my family loves to go for hikes. Sometimes it involves overnights. The talk of the family has been to want to bring a backpack along with tent and sleeping arrangements on an overnight hike in some great land around some lakes. I knew that our usual backpacks would not suffice, so when I saw this, I thought it would be perfect. Let's see how this measures up to what we need.

WHAT IS THIS BACKPACK LIKE?
The backpack has a very thick woven black fabric that is more like what you would find in a heavy jacket. It is not thin nylon that is sometimes found in backpacks. The black fabric is rugged. There is a sizeable gusset (10 inches) in the bottom which can be retracted with adjustable straps. These straps can hold a bedroll, small personal tent, or other similar things. The straps are pretty long so I am thinking the capacity is quite adaptable. That means you can pack a small personal tent AND bedroll or portable small cot (we have one that would fit perfectly here).

SIDE POCKETS
There are two small net pockets which can hold water bottles or similar things, and also side long zipped pockets which have cords on them for easy quick access. The zipped pockets are angled, but they measure 9 inches tall at widest point. The highest point is 10 inches.

ADJUSTABLE STRAPS
There are quite a few pair of adjustable straps:
- under backpack
-upper sides
-small circular straps at upper edge of back pocket
-from backpack to top of shoulder straps on the front (possibly can hold small roll of some sort)
-center of each shoulder strap to hook and hold backpack in place
-on padded waist belt to hold in place
-at base of padded waist belt to hold backpack to waistband for security
-in between shoulder straps in loop form to hang backpack from

BACK CENTER COMPARTMENT
This pocket has a tough handle on it so that you can lift the pack out when it is zipped. Inside there are three pocket compartments- two netted and one nylon. Compartment is 11 inches high, and pockets are- nylon: 7 1/2 high and nylon are 6 inches high and 5 inches wide each. The compartment itself is a little over 10 inches wide. The entire compartment has a double two way zipper which means that you can open it down each side or the entire way by sliding both heads to one side.

TOP BACK COMPARTMENT
This compartment is at the top of the back. It is about 9 x 9 approximately. This pocket has a place with a strap and a plastic/nylon hook so you can hang keys from it if you need to. The gusseting in the pocket allows bulky items to be put in this pocket. It is not too deep or too shallow to be practical.

PADDING AND SHOULDER STRAPS/HARNESS
The padding on this is great. The back itself is reinforced and very stiff, yet comfortable. It has plenty of padding on it for comfort while walking with a loaded pack. The straps have great padding on them as well. There is plenty of padding on the waist belt as well, with extra padding on the small of the back for comfort and ease of walking with support.

MAIN COMPARTMENT
This compartment is very deep and only has an elasticized pleated pocket in it which is on the reinforced back panel (the one that goes on your back when wearing the backpack). The entire compartment is approimately 22 inches in depth. The elasticized pocket inside is about 10 inches high. Width of back panel is about 12 inches. The compartment can extend up to 12 inches out if packed fully. There is another hook in this compartment to hang keys from etc.

WATER BAG
If you want to carry a water bag in the backpack, it would fit in here, and there is a little hole that you can slip the tube through for drinking. We do not use a water bag at this point so I can not comment on the usefulness of this feature.

WORKMANSHIP
This backpack seems to be made in top quality workmanship. The sewing is great, no loose threads, and all of the bindings and zippers seem to be in very well with no gaps or missed stitches.

OUR EXPERIENCE WITH THIS BACKPACK
So far, we have just had all day hikes with this- no bedroll or personal tent yet as it has been way too snowy and cold so far. However, as a backpack in general, we have packed this thing up well. I also did take it to a large fiber festival which required me to slip things rolled up into the straps and also to pack the backpack pretty well. It was easy to walk in and comfortable as well. I spent almost an entire day with it and it did not make me all stiff at the end of the day like some packs will do.

UPDATES
I will be updating this as we have a chance to use it over the summer for camping and serious overnight hiking as well.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Made with excellent workmanship, tough fabric, and well thought out, this backpack is great for hiking, even if a personal tent and/or bedroll or cot is desired to carry with you on a trek. Use of water pack is possible with this backpack although we have not used it in that capacity as of yet. The padding is comfortable and supportive and the backpack itself is easy to pack and carry if you are careful how you set it up for most balance and comfort as with any backpack.

MY RATING
This is five stars. It seems like it will meet our needs perfectly and I will update when I have more experiences to add to this review if applicable.

reviews.title: Above Average Backpack
reviews.text:
This is a good quality backpack that seems to be most useful for hiking and casual comping trips. At its current price, it is an excellent value for the money. All of the basics of a quality hiking pack are there with more than enough pockets and compartments for most and a cavernous main body that could probably hold most of the clothes I own in it. Because of it's huge size, I would not recommend it for urban use or to simply carry things around town. While it is definitely comfortable enough for such use, it is pretty cumbersome to carry around with you when it's empty and definitely isn't something you would want to wear while on a bike or climbing on and off a bus.

The material is of well above average quality. It definitely is not waterproof, but it is at least water resistant. The padded straps are extremely comfortable to use, even when carrying heavy loads. If there is any weak link in the construction, it would probably be in the stitching. The thread is fairly thick, but there are no double stitched areas at all, so I can see some of the seams on this backpack getting easily stressed when you are carrying especially heavy loads. The zippers and connectors are of about average quality. One detail that caught my eye was one of the larger zippers on the inside of the pack. It's actually stitched in backwards, which makes one compartment impossible to zip up, unless you were zipping it from the inside of the backpack! We all have one of those days, I guess. Someone definitely was asleep at the wheel in quality control this particular day.

The materials and construction are 100% Made in China. This definitely accounts for it's bargain price, but also explains some of the corners that were cut. This backpack is definitely adequate for casual use, but it certainly isn't something that you would want to use while climbing Mt. Everest or going on a professional expedition. For most of us though, this model will definitely do the job it was intended for and looks great while doing it.

reviews.title: Great vest, not that great a bottle
reviews.text:
I have a Camelback hydration pack that I love, but in the desert sun, it makes me a bit hot. I wanted a pack that covered less of my body, but still carried a nice 2L bottle to provide plenty of water for longer hikes, strolls or bike rides.

This pack is great. The lime green color is a bit "louder" than I would prefer, but it covers less of my torso, so I don't get overheated as easily. It’s made of a strong nylon material that seems to be waterproof. There are several highly reflective stripes that make you visible in low light.

The pouch for the hydration pack zips open nice and wide, so it's easier to get the bottle in and out. You thread the hose from the back to the front through the section where the back attaches to the strap, which is also easier to manage. There's room for a cell phone, sunglasses case and other small items in the pocket in front of the pouch in the back. However, if you have ice water in the pouch, they may get damp when condensation collects around the bag. There’s also the inconvenience of having to take the vest off or have someone get your stuff out for you that way. The crisscross cord in the back may allow you to carry a hiking pole, jacket or something else outside the pack.

I do miss having the clip for the mouthpiece I had on my Camelback vest. With this one, you have to reach down and grab the hose dangling at your side. There are clips on the front to allow you to hang a key chain or carabiners. There are adjustable straps to fit it to your body shape at the chest, from the bottom of the vest front to the back, and from the back around the waist.

The bottle is not that great. The opening is small, and it doesn’t have the handle to help you grasp and hold it open to fill it like my Camelback. I miss the quick-release valve at the bottom, too. For this one, you have to screw in the hose. The mouthpiece is fairly easy to use: You remove the white cap and pull the silicone mouthpiece up to open the valve. My Camelback bottle has a mouthpiece that you just bite down on to open the valve. Another issue is that the plastic seems a bit thin and may burst or spring a leak easier than my heavy-duty Camelback. One advantage this has over the other is the two openings at the top that allow you to hang the bag to air out.

If you don’t need a lot of stuff with you and want to stay cool during a hike, this vest may work for you. Nevertheless, I can’t really recommend the water bottle. You’d be better off getting a quality hydration bottle from another company. The price of about $25 seems fair. Yet, I think it would be better if these folks offered the vest by itself for about $15, and then you could buy a different 2L bottle.

reviews.title: Sadly broke before first use
reviews.text:
I am very sorry to be writing a negative review for this product - it's not my style - but I feel that I must in this case.

I bought this pot after doing a lot of research - I wanted something on the larger side, and on the affordable side, for a very small camping wood stove that I could use to cook food outdoors in a camping type of scenario. This pot arrived intact, in excellent condition, and I set it aside.

About two weeks after receiving it, I finally opened it and showed it to my family, who admired its lightness and the handle which snaps over the top. I walked out of the room, allowing my 6 year-old son to explore the item and move the handle himself.

Not long after, he came in looking very guilty - and confessed to me that he had broken my brand new pot. Now, my son is an active boy, and I wasn't there when it broke. But I don't think he terrorized my pot - he just opened and closed the handle. I think the major fault here lies in the construction - as you can see from the pictures, there are just tiny, gentle-looking welds that hold the handle onto the pot.

And so, given the nature of the item and its foldable handle, it was only a matter of time until this item was going to break, anyway. I am actually grateful this happened now, before I used this in a real time of need, only to possibly be scalded or have all my food simply fall away on the ground.

I debated giving this item 2 stars rather than just one, because the pot could probably still function for cooking (although I have not tested its integrity in a flame), but I decided that since it only survived about an hour outside the box, I just couldn't give it more than one star.

reviews.title: Don't spend 2x as much! This is great!
reviews.text: Great product at a fraction of the price

reviews.title: Excellent pot with one flaw, the handle should be rivetted.
reviews.text: I'm a big fan of the GSI Halulite boiler of the same size, but for times when I might want a little more durability, I picked up the Glacier stainless version. The one flaw this pot has is that, unlike the Halulite version, the handle is not rivetted to the pot, and as some reviewers have reported, the tiny spot welds can fail. I'm going to drill a hole and stick a stainless machine screw and nut through it until I can find and peen a rivet in place. So, one star off for that, but otherwise an excellent pot.

reviews.title: Perfect for my Intent, SQUEEZE THE HANDLE TOGETHER FOR EASY OPERATION
reviews.text:
I just received this and have not used in the field yet, however I have played with it a bit and it works great for my intended use.

For the longest time I have been trying to find a round pot/cup to fit the 8oz, red MSR backpacking propane canister with hopefully the stove on top, but really mostly I have been trying to find some sort of way to carry and protect these propane canisters.

To my excitement I came across these pots on amazon after figuring out how to type and search for what I had in my head. They are the absolute PERFECT diameter for the 8oz canister with a bandana wrapped around it so there is some cushion as well as no metal on metal. PERFECT FIT!

Unfortunately it is barely not long enough to fit the stove (inside its own little plastic carry box it came with) inside the pot with the canister, but if taken out it will fit. Otherwise the 2-5x8 inch MOLLE bottle carrier I got should fit the stove sitting on top of the pot outside of it, still cinched down by the bottle carrier.

Either way this STAINLESS STEEL pot/cup fits the bill perfectly for my intended use. GSI also offers this same 1.1L size pot in an alluminum version, and while it looks very nice you cannot set it on an open fire like you can with this one and the alluminum one is more expensive....

All around the quality, finish and function of this pot is exceptional. For those who say it is incredibly difficult to operate the handle, all you need to do is squeeze the handle together and it will move open and closed very easily and snap right into place. This is a big plus as it will effectively snap and lock the lid on in place. It will not be water or air tight but it will sit in place perfectly.

If I could make any recommendations it would be to offer this pot also in a 5x8 inch version, add a vented lid and honestly that would be it. The price for this 5x5 inch, 1.1L pot could also be a little less expensive, say around $19.99 regular price, otherwise it is perfect and still warrants a 5 star review.

I dont often give 5 star reviews even on the best of products. We have been aquiring more and more GSI brand items for camping, backpacking, survival and disaster preparedness over time due to the quality and price point for such.

BUY THIS POT AND DONT LOOK BACK!

reviews.title: Worth Every Penny
reviews.text:
I am a long term Maxpedition customer. I carried the Falcon II every day for nearly four years, packed to the gills. I needed to increase in size over the Falcon II and settled on the Falcon III since I was already comfortable with the design. It gives me enough additional capacity that it's not over-stuffed with my EDC gear. I prefer the design of the new zippers. I did like the separate zip up hydration bladder pocket of the Falcon II for CCW. But the same thing can be accomplished with the middle compartment on this pack. One addition I really like is the chest strap that keeps the shoulder straps in place. This pack is expensive, but it's worth every penny. I can highly recommend this for every day carry if you need a pack that will hold up over time. Maxpedition got it right again!

Update: January 29, 2107 - Still a great pack, no defects and still looks good. I will try to post an update again next year.

reviews.title: Sturdy bag, worth the investment
reviews.text:
I've owned the Falcon III for only two days, and I've had it on just one hike, and so far, I am VERY happy with the purchase. I ordered Khaki, which in the Amazon product listing, Khaki looks more like a desert sand color throughout, and the straps are the same color as the canvas. HOWEVER, what actually showed up is two-tone that leans more toward a green, and seems more like a different color Maxpedition offers, despite the label correctly saying Khaki. (I had earlier ordered the Falcon II in Khaki, and same thing, what showed up was very olive-like with tan straps.) I returned the Falcon II partly because of the wrong color, but also because I felt it was just too small for an adult, though it would be good for a kid or tween.

All of that said, I do like the Falcon III in whatever color they sent to me. Ha! Keep reading for actual review stuff...

STURDY
This is legit fabric. You can take it out of the box, open it up, and it will stand up on the floor all by itself! It's that rigid. The seams and sewing all seem very well done. The Molle feels really strong. The straps and buckles don't feet cheap. I think some people will probably say, "oh, the fabric is so hard and rough, I am sending this back." But the way I see it, you want something heavy duty that will take whatever you throw at it. I seriously can't imagine using this thing so much that it wears a hole in the fabric. That seems impossible. I think you could fill this up and drag it on the dirt behind a truck, and... no problems.

SIZE
Okay, I am a 6-foot big dude and probably pushing 285 lb. The pack is easy to put on and easy to take off. I wasn't squirming or stretching or contorting myself to get it on or off. The overall size is great. During my hike today, I never felt like it was this tiny thing on my back... and I never felt like it was some ginormous camp-in-the-woods-for-a-month obnoxious pack. It just seemed perfect in size. The bottom of the pack hung down to just above my butt. And again, I was super glad I returned the Falcon II so that I could have the larger Falcon III. I could easily walk, hike, bike or travel with the Falcon III. It would be a great bag to fill up with essentials and get on an airplane without checking larger bags.

POCKETS & STORAGE
The main large pocket is big and I could very easily put my laptop computer in here. The large pocket includes a pouch where you can drop in your water bladder, and there are two covered holes (one on either size) for your water hose to come out. In that water pocket, if you didn't want to put water in there, it's big enough for a small chromebook, or a book or notepad. Also in the main pocket, there is a netted pocket that is not zippered. I put two books in there. There's plenty of space left for a jacket or blanket some extra small clothes, etc.
The middle-sized pocket is just as deep as the big main pocket. This middle area has no organization. I used this space for my small medical kit and a very large 1.5 liter water bottle. And there was quite a bit of empty space left for more stuff.
The outside pocket on top is not very deep and has no organization inside. It's big enough for a sandwich and a granola bar or two, but not much else. On my hike today I had a bag of peanuts, three granola bars and my sunglasses.
The outside pocket on the bottom is a much larger external space and it has more organization for pens, knife, flashlight, and a hanger for keys. There's also a rear pouch inside. There was some extra space, but I would not put anything in there that is fragile (like a phone) since your knife and keys, could scratch it.
My only complaint here is that I am jealous of other bags that have more organization in the main compartments. If I was the designer, I guess I would have added a zipper to at least one of the compartments in the primary space.... and for sure I would add another pouch (or two) in the secondary space. But maybe Maxpedition's M.O. is that they want customers to buy more pouches to store stuff internally, and externally via molle.

BUCKLES & STRAPS
The main shoulder straps are padded and comfortable. They have no storage on them, though there are D-rings and molle so you can add pouches, etc. The padding on the shoulder straps is the same material as what's on the main back pad.
The sternum buckle is plenty long to fit me (again, I am a big guy). I used it during my hike just to keep the shoulder straps in place. I never hiked without it connected, so I can't say how the whole thing hangs without the sternum strap connected.
The waist strap just hangs and cannot be stored or put away. That's kinda weird. Anyway, I hiked without putting it around me. I just buckled the two sides together and let it hang. That was never uncomfortable and really I never felt it or thought about it.
The compression straps all around are good and also don't get in the way. You can compress two straps from back to front. And you can connect one compression strap from top to bottom. I think they did a good job with this.

AIR FLOW & MAIN PADDING
I don't know what you call the main pad that actual touches your back, but that whole area is a black net finish on top of the padding (same as the shoulder straps). If anything on this bag is going to ever tear, it's that black netting. But it felt perfectly soft and comfortable on my back during my hike today. It was only about 74 degrees, so not hot enough to sweat my butt off. So I can't tell about the air flow. But so far it seems fine. My back certainly never felt wet.

WHAT ELSE?
I guess that's about all I can say. I am a pretty frugal guy and it took some convincing to make myself spend $150 on a backpack. But I have lived long enough to know that it's probably a good investment and will likely be the last backpack I have to buy. It's certainly not going to fall apart like the $30 bag I bought in 2017 (multiple ripping problems and straps disintegrating!) So would I rather buy a new $30 backpack every few years, or just spend $150 now on a quality back that I can get used to and have for a decade or more?

reviews.text:
[[VIDEOID:670390d5f4bbbcd1c8a0c687f3650946]] Let me start by saying that I am a person that does a lot of research before buying an item. I don't spend on a whim. It may take me weeks or a month before making that buying commitment. I look for something that has all the features I need.
I was looking to replace my air Jordan sling that I've had for at least 15 years , maybe longer. First choice was another air Jordan but I could not get the same style..so I started hunting.
This brand seemed to fit my needs. Had many of the same feature as my old backpack..and this has a bottle holder which my old one did not have. BONUS :) So I waited till prime day and got this for 10dollars cheaper . Oh ,and the reviews were decent .
Well it arrived today and I couldn't be more disappointed. This is really small for my needs. Measurements on this are embellished. Reviews said this was great for a day trip or hike but honestly if you just wear a Tshirt and shorts you would be ok. I wanted to fit work clothes and my lunch in this bag but that isn't happening.
There are many pockets but let's be honest, you can only fit so much inside this bag. Extra pockets don't give you more space, they provide just separation.
We shall see how the durability of this is. No way it will give me 15 years as I'm pretty rough on my bag as it goes everywhere I go. It's hard letting go of a good pair of shoes or a bag or any fashion you have had for many years cause it's hard to replace something so durable. I'm sure many have had that experience.
Overall this is just to small for my needs as you can see in the picture. The measurements are a stretch. Durability we will see and I will update.
1 WEEK later......no issues with the bag. I have been gentle as far as overstuffing it. The size issue is muy inconvenient. Many issues on that topic but just one......I work outdoors and head to work with a hoodie cause its chilly in the a.m. the hoodie wont fit in the bag when the weather warms and i only have a shirt, lunchbag, phone/charger, misc stuff already in it.. Reading the comments , This makes me curious what kind of day trip people are taking in order to use this bag in that fashion..

reviews.title: PEOPLE To avoid FRAYING learn to melt the raw cut edges.
reviews.text:
A bit too thin for most of my major utilitarian packs and duffles and bags. Might work for lighter weight small bags. However having said that I'm making 6 classic grocery brown paper bags out of nylon pack cloth coated fabrics. The colors will be pretty much a match actually. But thought I might add some charm with different colored handles. Even though I need a strong handle for a grocery bag these are far better than the paper glued on ones that almost always seem to fail me if I'm carrying a dozen or two eggs. Anyway I'll mange to use some of this up for that and also for a technique I developed for making fancy hidden zipper closures for ultra plush and high piled throw pillows. I actually buy 1.5" to 1" similar webbing knowing how thin it is for the sole purpose of using with the pillow closure. Anyway I could get by with 1" and looks like I will since I bought a lot of this in various colors. I wasn't paying close attention so It's my fault I bought so much and also bought any at all. Yes the description and photos aren't announcing how thin this is but many reviewers have posted that info. So I guess I was in a hurry. I love the colors but also do have some TRUE webbing on it's way and tubular too which is more what I need for back packs and heavy duty tote bags. This would never do for handles for those items. Maybe adding some support in hidden areas of construction however. I also wuld not use this for leads or collars or hanesses for pets if you make those this is really on the light weight side.
The edges melt well on this so get out your bic lighters, candles of just about any size and or even your gas stove and wood burner tip. The woodburners not my cup of their tips just get gummed up and difficult to clean it off. It took me years to get through all the left over pieces of tapered candles from our wedding in the 70's. And by the time I had or we had my husband sews too we had more partial burned down tapers to use. But any candle can work. But I'm thinking more along the lines of when you are making down jackets or sleeping bags etc. where you have miles of fabric edges to melt. I keep real bic lighters in my sewing drawer because I have trouble with most cheaper knock offs. Hubby can use any of him but his hands are stronger. I also keep a tea light in a plastic bag handy just in case I'm doing a bunch of pieces at once too. Anyway the key to prevent fraying is the tried and true method of melting the raw cut ends including the piece on the roll which probably will fray too. In case I didn't mention it earlier I would not use this nylon tape for leads, collars, leashes, harnesses etc. for pets. Ok maybe a tiny tea cup pet but this is not the usual weight for those items. I'll definitely pay more attention in the future to avoid this problem again. I think I ordered 6 different colors. OOPS. I don't sew for money so it's going to be a long time before I run out. A good length of 45 feet or 15 yards as it's the option I bought all on.

If you've ever had to stow your gear with other travelers, you'd appreciate having a brightly colored bag like this each time you went to retrieve it. If you prefer a more subdued color, this bag also comes in blue and black options. The main compartment of this daypack is also roomy and comes with a laptop pocket with decent padding at the back. The only things I would change about this bag would be by adding some more padded reinforcement at the bottom, and include a rain cover that would protect the open top compartment above the brand logo. All the same, I can still get a great deal of use out of this bag as a lightweight daypack or overnight bag.

reviews.title: The options are endless
reviews.text: This is a fantastic pack. I wanted something large enough to fit overnight gear in, yet is not bulky and has options for both summer and winter items. This pack is extremely comfortable, with the NDM function working flawlessly. The hip pockets are massive, allowing for plenty of snacks or other items. Additionally, there is a small opening between the pocket and the hip belt, which I was able to carry an axe in and not weigh down my pants at all. There are two zipper pockets on the side above each water bottle pocket, and these are quite deep for plenty of options. There is a sleeve along the back panel for bladders, or cut z-lite pads. In that same area is a “hidden” zipper which is also extremely deep, going just about to the bottom of the pack. The main compartment is a roll top, with waterproof lining on the inside. It is extremely spacious, yet does not expand the size of the pack tons when stuffed. On the front-bottom of the pack is another small pocket- however these items will rest on the bottom of the main compartment when the pack in on the ground, so any fragile items in here may not hold up well. It was large enough for me to stuff a puffy inside, so plenty of room there as well. The side straps are useful-ish, with the option to cinch them down for the pack to fit better, or they offer a small bit of room for stuffing items. With some effort, I was able to squeeze a small shovel between a few of these, securing it to the outside of the pack. The front does offer a few small straps for clipping items to the outside as well. Overall supremely pleased with this pack, and I’m excited to give it a go in the dry months with some trail running!

reviews.title: Great Little Hydration Pack
reviews.text: I bought this for short (~3 hr) summer hikes in the mid-Atlantic region, where I need a lot of water.  The 2L hydration pack was perfect for that.  The bladder works well, the connector to the hose is solid.  The only "trick" was that I have to thread the hose through all of the holders on the strap and into the bag itself before connecting it to the bladder, since the mouthpiece is too large to thread though.  The bladder sits in an insulated section of the pack, so it holds the cool temperature pretty well, even better if you dump some ice in before you leave home.  What I really like is how much other stuff fits in the pack:  tissues, hand sanitizer, headband, my huge wallet, and a hat (and I don't even stuff it full).  The laces on the outside of the pack would even accommodate a light jacket.  There are two hip pockets, neither of which is large enough for my iPhone 8 plus without having to really work it in there, but it great for chapstick and my car keys (there is no clip inside for keys, as I have in other packets, but one of the hip band pockets works just fine for this)!  This is an ideal alternative to my large Osprey pack when I need to take a lot of water with me on a hike and I don't want to wear a large pack.  The pack also comes with a little flexible cleaner for the hose and with an extra gasket for the hose-bladder connection.  Great buy!

reviews.title: Bladder failed at a critical moment
reviews.text: I purchased this hydration backpack with the 3L water bladder in mid April, in preparation for a long US roadtrip with several visits to national and state parks. With lots of hiking in hot weather, I needed a reliable hydration source. Unfortunately this product wasn’t it. I tested the bladder system at home, and it seemed OK. However, the bladder didn’t survive its first real world test. In Canyonlands, Utah, with 100+ degree weather, two things happened: (1) the suction end got punctured within minutes. It still worked and didn’t leak, so I kept on using it throughout the day. (2) At the end of the day, back at the hotel, when I tried to refill the bladder I couldn’t get the bladder seal off. The hard plastic handle/seal doesn’t budge at all, and it almost seems as if it has fused closed (I don’t think that’s possible, but the reality is I can’t slide it at all, and yes, I am doing it in the right direction.) Bottom line: I am at the beginning of a series of hikes, left without this key component of my hydration system (fortunately I have backups, though I’ll miss having a hydration backpack/water bladder, and it’s beyond the return window, so I’m out of money as well. I know that the vast majority of the reviews are positive (that’s why I bought this item!), but based on my experience I cannot recommend this product. One star from me.

reviews.text:

It is basically a kids version of a gopack, with underwear, extra socks, cereal bars, leggings, facemasks (against air pollution and smoke in the event of wildfires, not to go to the store), water bottle, walkie talkie, gotenna and some other tricks. It doesn't replace the bigger version, that is packed to evacuate, or the duffle bag in the car, but in case we are stranded, there is enough to stay a day or two. Be prepared, be ready.
The quality is good. Even the zippers seem to be better than from what I experienced with cheaper bags in the past. The velcro is strong, and the sling has extra loops, which is great. Many sling-bags leave the sling space unused or just add an extra zipper.
I am giving this product five stars. On a budget this is a good bag. Clearly not as good as a product that is specifically designed to take it into the field, but my guess is that it can withstand a kid for about a year. More if not used daily. Neat: The hidden zipper at the bottom!

reviews.title: Packs up well
reviews.text: This cook set was added in and is being tested in my camping kit. This is a good size for two people and is not suited for a larger group. It packs up nicely in its little bag that has a hook and loop strap, I like that. I attempted to test it out at home before bringing it on a short trip. The way the handles are designed to fold in, keep the pan from sitting flat on my glass top which has the handle propping it up a bit, but isn’t an issue on my camp stove. They heat up fairly quick and work fine for cooking. They cleaned up nicely, but will get scratched up a bit but thats outdoor life. I’m not testing these out over direct flame as I don’t feel they will fair well after a while but for stove use, they are fine. If your wanting open flame, I’d use cast iron. The handles work pretty good and keep your hands from getting burned up. Time will tell if the handles continue to hold up when weighted with water and food, They are a bit flimsy but I’ve seen worse. This kit is light but they are heavier than some Titanium sets that are for ultralight packing, this does not bother me as I don’t really do that type of camping. Overall I think this is a nice little set for two. I’d recommend these.

reviews.title: Very Good Aluminum Cookware
reviews.text:
This is a great little set to my cookware collection for camping. I have products from GSI, Snow Peak and Sea To Summit and this one is a great addition to the collection.

I included pictures with a lighter so you can get an idea for size.

The pots nest in each other well and the carrying case is brilliant - it has a zip top and a velcro closure so you could loop it onto you pack on the exterior to save space, or if the pots were still wet from cleaning. The integrated handles are quite nice and stick out far enough from the pot that they don't get hot from the stove, and also cool down quickly due to the silicone handles.

Being aluminum, they are light (although, not as light as a titanium set) and dry very quickly - something every backpacker enjoys so you can pack up camp and move along. They are NOT non-stick so stir frequently, otherwise you'll have some soaking and scrubbing to do.

reviews.title: Well made, but wastes side and poor organization.
reviews.text:
First off, the bag is well made and I checked the construction and it has suitable reinforcements and bar tackings at all stress points. It has that typical chemical stink of all Chinese-made rubberized products. Yuck!! What baffles me is the organization or lack of organization.

The main compartment for the boots is cavernous and a lot of that space is wasted because you can't access it unless you want to put things in with your wet boots. Maybe put an extra dry bag in the between the boots.

To access the central compartment from above, you have to go through the helmet storage area and at the bottom there is a partial zipper to give you access to the wider compartment below. Why didn't they put a full width zipper in there? You would have to take everything out of the top compartment, open the parcel zipper and then fish around in the larger compartment below to get access to your stuff. You won't have any view in there.

Why did that bag from the top not fill up the entire space between the boots, but only a half of it? The larger compartment that contains the boots should have had more of the upper bag project into the space between the boots. Now that space is wasted.

The two front compartments have no organizational divides in them at all. Everything will just all slide around and settle to the bottom. A few elastic nettings on the side would have helped to keep smaller items in an accessible place without having everything mix together.

Why the two large slash pockets on each side? Do they not know that people will be using this in the snow? These will definitely become snow catchers should it snow or should you fall. And then things fall out. When the snow melts, guess what's going to get wet. Everything. Snow catchers do not belong on any skiing gear, ever, full stop.

I don't know about you, but I can never imagine skiing with a 65 l bag on my back without a waist strap. Why did they leave that off? Why is there no front handle, only a top?

Oh well, so close to being a useful bag. I give it four stars and I'm returning it because I want a five star piece of equipment. For 10 bucks more I can get it.

reviews.title: Futuristic looking, easy to use.
reviews.text:
This is a really cool looking coffee maker. Very futuristic, especially with the red light while brewing.
It's a little bit larger than my ninja coffee bar. Slightly taller and slightly wider. I ordered this to replace the Ninja because the Ninja keeps giving me the five beeps of death and will not brew or clean anymore. This one is a totally different setup and doesn't have all the bells and whistles, but makes a solid cup of coffee.
The water goes in the back compartment, filter and coffee grounds in the front. Very simple instructions, easy to understand, presented well.
The options are bold or normal brew coffee, timed coffee making, keep warm, and makes up to 12 cups.
The fact that the coffee carafe and be accessed within a 180° range is a great and helpful feature.
It does not specifically say it will brew a single cup, but since I drink a 20 oz mug of coffee every morning and not a tiny cup, that is not an issue. It handled the 20 oz perfectly fine.
I am really pleased with this coffee maker, I recommend it.
EDIT: After using this for a couple weeks, I've got a couple more observations. Unless I'm missing something, you have to add water each time for the exact amount of coffee you want - I see no setting for serving size options. I generally put the amount of water I want in the mug that I want to use and pour it into the water compartment. Would be nice to fill the water and just hit a size button.
Also, there is a lot of condensation at the top of the grounds compartment, but i just tap the lid before I open it and that takes off most of the condensation.
I removed a star because of the inability to choose brew size.

reviews.text:
This is a work of art. It’s very easy to use, excellent quality. The weight of the copper feels strong and thick to me.

It’s feels like I’m taking an exotic vacation to an ancient world as I use this to make coffee.

The best thing about this, beyond it’s beauty and the lovely experience using it, is that it makes a delicious cup of coffee.

I’ve tried many different ways to make coffee, and prior to this, my favorite was a simple French press or an old school percolator, which I still like.

This, however, this beautiful copper briki, is amazing.

I don’t really understand it, but the coffee is not acidic, not bitter, and is so smooth that no cream is needed.

I found a recipe online that includes ground cardamom and sugar brewed in with the coffee. I make my coffee with these ingredients and it’s so delicious. I also add a splash of vanilla, and I made vanilla sugar with cane sugar, and this, I think, adds a bit to the delicious flavor of this coffee.

A small amount of coffee goes a long way with this, which is another plus.

I can’t see myself going back to making coffee the ways I used to.

This copper pot has won me over.

If I go anywhere for an extended period, I may have to take the smaller version of this pot with me.

This pot I am reviewing is the 28 oz pot.

I also have the 14 oz pot, which is good for two or three people, in small cups.

It’s rich and smooth and delicious, and I don’t feel that I want more than the small espresso sized cup of coffee. Even a demitasse cup is great.

I would certainly recommend this company, Dede’s copper coffee pots. It’s quality copper and the pot arrived in perfect shape.

reviews.title: Failed on first use - Updated
reviews.text:
First use the unit heated too temp of 99c shut off okay great. welll not great lifted it up and hot water was leaking out the bottom into my cup holder. Now has steam in the window and controls don’t work. I’m pretty certain the relief valve failed to open. It’s possible I just got a bad one. Trying another will update:

Update:
Purchased another unit and this one seems fine However I Removed the check ball out of the silicone seal in the cap. I’m very certain this is what caused my first failure with not venting pressure during the unit coming to a boil consequently making the lower body seals start leaking. It’s actually safer with it removed abit of steam comes out when it nears boil but that’s better than opening a pressurized vessel as many have encountered. With the check ball removed mine goes to 99c shuts off and I can open it immediately with no boil flare up. I’ve tested it about two dozen times and currently traveling the east coast so far it’s not failed. Keep in mind if your heating to a boil and removed your pressure check ball it will steam some out the hole on the cap it’s not much you may not even notice it but be aware. I fill mine to the max fill line and it has never spit water out the hole. Anyway be careful of any steam!

I’m giving 4 stars as of now due to the pressure relief flaw

reviews.title: Get off the fence!
reviews.text:
Edit: February 13, 2022

I knocked 3 stars off my original rating, it doesn't heat the water properly. If I don't use hot water, I'll get lukewarm coffee. It's a shame because otherwise this thing is amazing. Blerg.

This is my second grind and brew coffee machine. My first, the Viatne Mini Grind & Brew, which for all ts fickleness served me well for 2+ years. It too had a good amount of critical ratings but I stuck with it and was rewarded with freshly ground & brewed coffee every morning and have zero regrets.

The Power XL Grind & Go is an improvement in almost every area. It has less parts, is more efficient and is not as fickle as the Viante.

It takes about 6 minutes for the grind & brew cycle to complete and yes it makes noise (as does anything grinding up stuff!). It does not have a hot plate so you'll want to time it so that you're ready to drink your deliciousness when its done brewing.

The Viante had a hot plate and to be honest I never really let my coffee sit for very long seeing as how it was only a single cup. I mean, it's not like you need to keep an entire pot of coffee warm.

Anyway, you must make sure the notches are properly aligned after you load the beans in the grinder but otherwise, I've found it pretty much idiot proof.

This is a cool little machine which has taken the concept of the single serve grind & brew coffee maker and improved on it immensely in my opinion. No, it has not been perfected quite yet but it's getting there!

reviews.title: An Elegant Start To Every Day
reviews.text:
At first look, this thing is tiny, but it's also cute as a button, and it works like a charm. I actually have both sizes, this 155 size, for single cups, and the 185 size for 2-3 cups.

At first I thought the 185 size would be ok for a single cup, and it is, but the 155 is tapered in such a way that it holds the smaller filter more straight up and down, giving a more even bed for the smaller amount of coffee grounds needed for only one cup, as well as letting the pouring spout be right at the level of the bed, rather than way above it.

Let me put it this way, it's simply a more elegant way of preparing one cup of coffee, and after all, that's really what I'm after, a small ritual to start my day that involves a bit of science, a bit of art, and a bit of mystery.

It would be easy to use a coffee maker, but I've opted for something that takes me back to the essence of what coffee brewing is all about, having total control over the entire brewing process. I love the thoughtful design of the Kalita system, the way the filters are designed to keep the brewing coffee away from the side wall, the way the flat bottom with 3 holes gives a precise bed of grounds that allows for perfectly even extraction, and the nicely built stainless steel dripper that is lovely to use, and a breeze to clean up.

So,how does the coffee taste? Well, that depends on so many things. At this level, the dripper is merely one part of the process, including where and how the beans are grown, the roasting process, the age of the roasted beans, the type of grind, the heat of the water, and finally, the method of extraction, which in this case is the Kalita 155 Wave Dripper. Use exceptional beans, roasted properly and used quickly, along with the proper grind done at the time brewing, and the Kalita 155 will deliver a cup of coffee that celebrates everything that coffee has to offer.

For me, the Kalita 155 Wave Dripper is one of those little things that makes each day just a bit more special.

reviews.title: Recommended. But read through all of my notes beginning in October 2020.
reviews.text:
Gabi Master A – June 2021

I am now a HUGE fan of this device. Please read through all of my updates as they will show how I have evolved my use of the Gabi Master A.

Note: The Gabi distribution holes WILL clog. They’re tiny and any sediment, etc. may clog. So always test it by pouring some water into it without the paper filter or coffee to make sure water is passing through each hole. If not, try blowing it out or wiping the holes with a sponge. Just be sure you have correct flow before making your coffee each morning. It just takes a minute.

Original Comment - Gabi Master A.
One thing. The first time you assemble you’re gonna be nervous about that push hard to fit, the water bottle and water spout, cause there aren’t notches to fit, it’s a compression fit. So just push it down. I was afraid of breaking it the first time but I took a chance and it worked.
Kalita 155 which I didn’t have, so I trimmed a 185.
I’ll report on coffee quality after playing with it for a week.

Update 1 - This is kind of interesting. Noting a lukewarm cup of coffee, I poured 210 F boiling water through the unit with no coffee but with the paper filter. The water temp in the carafe measured 145 F.

Update 2 - Moving into the next brew and experiments. You know? I’m beginning to think that the Rao Swirl is preferable for coffee saturation to this device (re:temperature drop)...

Update 3 - Something is not right. I'm thinking the Gabi is more of a “fun gadget”. Check this out. Normally with the Rao Swirl, we’d see a nice even bed of coffee. Look at the results of the Gabi. 36 grams, 576 ml. Water temp after extraction. 150 F. Flavorwise, thinner but tasty.

Update 4 - 15 g at 160 ml. Uneven and incomplete extraction. As noted by some, their recommendation for ratio is different than SCAA standards, per their brochure so keep this in mind.

Update 5 - You know, as I settle in with really evaluating today’s extraction, it is flavorful. It makes me want to keep working with this device. Maybe it is irrelevant if the coffee bed doesn’t look like it normally would.

Update 6 - I’m now adding a swirl (aka the Rao Swirl) after the first pour that they recommend to soak the beans. I’ve now tried several of the recommended coffee and water ratios they recommend in the booklet that comes with the device. I’m starting to like some of the flavor profiles. But not all. I think I may be turning into a fan for this gadget. Time will tell. Gonna take a break and then come back with a four way test with standard Kalita and two grind sizes and then the same grind sizes with the Gabi Master A. For a side by side comparison. Will update later.

Update 7 - I’m still torn on whether to recommend or not. I did a serious, controlled experiment with 12 g coffee and 200 ml. I did two different grind settings on my Baratza (extreme settings of 10 and 24 to really push the envelope as it were) and made coffee with a standard Kalita 185. Then I did the same grinds with the Gabi. Whereas with only my Kalita, the coffee was acceptable with both grinds, slight differences in acidity but not significant (more bitterness with the finer grind), the fine grind was not good with the Gabi. There was a paper-y taste that I can't explain. Because I had rinsed the filters in all cases. (Note: if you are starting out, do a water taste test. Run some water through a Kalita filter, about 100 ml, and pour 100 ml straight from your kettle. Cool and taste both. If you can't tell the difference, rinsing you paper filter probably isn't necessary before brewing...having said that I always rinse my filter cause I've always done that). Only the coarser grind was flavorful and actually nice. Thus, my recommendation is to buy the Gabi if you want to add a coolness factor to your morning brew and don’t mind working really hard to find the sweet spot. Otherwise, just stick with your standard Kalita pour over method and save $35.

Update 8 – Oh heck, just buy it and have fun with it.

Update 9 - That paper taste. So, I’m having coffee with a friend and his first question is “is there a significant temperature drop in the device because water temper contributes to the paper taste”. The aha moment. This is what is happening. So it is imperative that you rinse the Kalita filter with boiling hot water after putting it in the basket in order to warm up the plastic a little and remove the paper taste.

Update 10 - one final test. I pulled out my Kalita and added 18 grams of coffee to it. I set up my scale and 3 glasses. Using my scale to keep track, I did three pours of 100 ml each. The first 100 would be the strongest of course and the third would be the weakest and possibly the most sour. Note: I did not zero out the scale for the second and third pours. I tasted all three. I then did exactly the same but with the Gabi.

I let them cool. And tasted and compared.

There was a more “paper” taste to the third cup of the Gabi than with the Kalita. But it was also thinner but less sour. The first cup of the Gabi was more intense than the Kalita, more syrupy, and more coffee components were extracted, almost like what one would see with a phin extraction. Combing cups one and two of the Gabi resulted in a stronger more intense coffee. I didn’t use the third cup in both cases. I think I may have liked the less intense Kalita extraction. But with this last experiment, I am reverting back, adding a star and giving the Gabi a recommendation. Once more.

Update 11 - As of June 2021, I am now a fan, and recommend the Gabi without hesitation. Into a double wall Kalita carafe, I set up the Gabi with the white Kalita 155 filter paper that I pre-rinsed just enough so that any paper powder was rinsed out but the ridges weren't collapsed. Do your rinsing in the Gabi as the walls will keep the Kalita filter rigid during rinsing. I then grind 24 grams of coffee with my Baratza Virtuoso Plus on a #16 setting (note: when I get a new bag of coffee, I always do three tests of 12g coffee to 200 ml water at grind settings of 10, 16, and 22. I do these with a Kalita 185 and no Gabi. I then taste each extraction and decide which grind produced the tastiest coffee). I pour 400 ml (that's the SCAA 16:1 ratio) of water in 3 pours. And as I've noted, I am well pleased with the results. Additional note: I'd recommend also buying the Gabi Master B. I use that with a Kalita 185 and 36 grams of coffee to 600 ml water.

reviews.text:
I've had a Rancilio Rocky for over 12 years, moved it with me from US to Europe (where I used it with a transfomer) and back, use it 3-4 times every day, never had the slightest problem, no parts replaced, no service needed. Unit does not need frequent cleaning -- once a month suffices with my volume. Only one very minor complaint: the bean hopper will frequently stop feeding beans: espresso roast typically produces "greasy" beans that stick together and the hopper bottom has a rather low cover, so beans stick together and don't go through (trivial to remedy: remove the lid of the hopper and just stir the beans).
Side comment: I drink only espresso; the doser is of no use for espresso (I never grind more than what I need for one dose and the doser does not do well with fine grinds, which tend to stick to the sides and bottom). Several years after I bought my Rocky, Rancilio introduced a doser-less version, which I would recommend for espresso.

reviews.title: It's beautiful, well made, iconic, and bad at coffee making
reviews.text:
So well made.
So stylish.
Great packaging.
Great materials.
It's perfect.
Except it's much much worse as a moka pot, than the Bialetti Venus that costs about 1/4.

At the end of the day, the latching mechanism doesn't work as well as a screw top on the default mocha pots. It's both harder to use, and doesn't seal nearly as well. I spent a week trying to get this to produce coffee without spitting boiling water. In the end, I failed, gave up, and returned it.

Yeah, there are tricks, hacks, techniques....but. Why? At it's best it'll match the Venus. At worst it costs more, is more temperamental, and makes worse coffee.

Great art piece.
Not a great coffee making device.

reviews.title: This is the ultimate Moka pot
reviews.text:
I live within walking distance from three roasters. I can get amazing expresso whenever I want. But, I like to roast unique beans and brew at home. Sometimes I use an AeroPress. But, most of the time I use the Alessi. It is NOT an Espresso maker. It is its own kinda animal. I've own several Moka pots over the years and the Richard Sapper design takes it to a new level. The quick release handle is literally a snap to clean.

To brew I preheat filtered water before filling the bottom reservoir. Main difference with an espresso machine is to back off from compressing the grounds in the porto filter. The main action is more convection than pressure. So, the water needs room to flow. You'll know you have the right grind, compactness, and heat, is when it only starts to sputter after it is nearly full. If it sputters too soon, then it means that the water is having a hard time making its way through the grounds. Turn up the heat too high, and the first part of the extraction will over cook. After a few tries, it will become second nature. And what you'll have is the perfect Moka cup.

reviews.title: Functional, beautiful and stainless steel.
reviews.text: I’ve been using bialetti stovetop “espresso” makers since 1985. This is the first time I shifted. Good move. I love that this product is made of stainless steel (though even while not using too high a flame the bottom section of the pot is yellowing just barely). I think this makes a better, and slightly larger and stronger cup of coffee than a bialetti 6. I like the design and very much like the locking mechanism. Looks good, works better. Just a great purchase even for the cost.

reviews.title: Love this super simple infusion system
reviews.text:
This infusion system is very simple to use. Just put the seal on the filter, insert the filter in your mason jar (1 or 2 qt), add coffee, add water, put on the mason jar lid, and let sit 12 to 24 hours. Remove the filter,
and you have your coffee.

The filter is easy to empty and clean and easy to store. I like that no paper filter is needed, it works great without. The silicone funnel folds up flat for storage. I did not need the funnel for making coffee but will come in handy when I try some of the alcohol infusions mentioned in the little recipe pamphlet included in the set.

The coffee tasted good. I prefer light dilution of water or steamed milk,not the 50/50. I highly recommend this product. It is so much better than the complicated set ups I have tried in the past for making cold brew. I really prefer the lack of acidity when making coffee this way.

reviews.title: Not ideal for cold brew coffee, but has many uses
reviews.text:
I got this with making cold brew coffee in mind. I have a French press, but this is a little larger and I prefer glass. After making it in this I dont think it is ideal for me, but it has many uses.

Here are some pros about the product:

-The jar is wide mouth, very large
- good quality, glass and bpa free
-It comes with a metal screen filter, screw on top, and a large collapsible funnel
-many uses (coffee, tea, fruit infused drinks)
- dishwasher friendly
- comes with a little pamphlet that gives you tips on how to make drinks

And the cons:
-No tool or way to get push/squeeze all the water out of the beans
-You could only put a certain amount of beans in there limiting the strength of the coffee
-metal screen gets smaller as it goes down which also effects the coffee to water ratio.

I filled my beans and water up to the top and the coffee turned out too watery and not strong enough for my taste.

Overall a good brewer. But instead of using it mainly for coffee, I will use it for tea or fruit infused drinks!

reviews.title: All Over the Countertop
reviews.text:
Wow, I’m amazed that this machine has anything but single star reviews.

First off, when I opened the box it felt possible that it had been opened before but I just wasn’t sure. After it was all on my counter it dawned on me that the cord was loose, so of course it had been opened and possibly tried before. Next I saw a water spot, so yes, someone had tried it out prior to me.

But I decided that since it was on my counter I’d try it. I had just had to return TWO other espresso/coffee makers for already being opened, so it was all getting old. I was willing to keep it IF it worked well.

It didn’t.

So, the bigger issue and why only ONE STAR.

It doesn’t shut off!! It’s insane to even think a manufacturer would create an espresso machine that just keeps letting out water, from the attached water tank. I turned away while cooking breakfast, only to look over and see coffee overflowing in the cup and on to the countertop. So bizarre. Sending it back.

reviews.title: Makes a great cup of coffee, but is big and bulky.
reviews.text: This coffee maker makes a delicious cup of coffee, however takes some getting used to the style. In our kitchen we have cabinets above our countertops and it’s a tight fit because it’s so large. The reservoir that you fill up is different. It feels like the tank of a steam cleaner and takes some getting used to. It’s nice that you can adjust the plate temperature as well. The plate stays on for awhile as well. It has a timer which counts down the time till it turns off. You have the option of using the included reusable filter or using standard paper filters. There is also a brew button on front and side, so you can position different ways on your counter. It’s nice, just a different design that will take some getting used to and it’s a bit pricey.

reviews.title: Love this coffee maker - no complaints
reviews.text:
I really have no complaints about this coffee maker. I love that the water tank comes off and has a handle. It is so much easier to fill it that way than dumping cups of water into the maker. This also makes it a lot easier to keep clean.

The basket for the coffee is high quality as well and holds even finer grinds. I think my favorite feature is the dosage ladder in the basket. It has a graduated "staircase" on the inside where each step is numbered. This helps you remember how many scoops of coffee you put in! I always would forget and have my pot too weak or too strong. This is such a simple feature. I don't know why more coffee makers don't adopt it.

The coffee maker itself has basic features like auto-programming, a heating plate for up to two hours, and it also has a bold setting. The bold setting slows down the rate at which water moves through the beans and enhances flavor extraction. I use this feature when I buy small batch coffee.

reviews.text: [[VIDEOID:b0c3e3483cf4209ab76c6cca26dbafff]] Nespresso machines are without a doubt the best. Bought a DeLonghi Lattissima 6 years ago, it’s still going strong. Always liked the VertuoLine and it’s crema feature, so treated myself to this machine. It’s flawless, perfect cup every time. reviews.title: Stores its own used pods, nice crema in each cup. Limited flavor options & proprietary pods
reviews.text:
Several years ago, we had a Nespresso Dolce Gusto machine that made great coffee. It also leaked constantly and after having the warranty replace three units, we went to the Kuerig. No mechanical problems, but the coffee is nothing to brag about. This new Vertuo machine is definitely more sturdy and better made than our original Nespresso unit.

Using this maker is a pleasure for several reasons. The physical footprint is smaller than our big Kuerig, so it gives me back a bit of counter space. The coffee is the exactly right temperature and has that lovely crema froth on top. This crema is the result of the high pressure the machine uses. The various samples of the different flavors offered for the Vertuo have all been good. None have come out bitter or weak. My favorite trick though, is the fact that when your coffee has finished brewing, you never need touch a hot, dripping pod. As soon as you open the top, the used pod swooshes off into the left side container. You just remove the container and empty it directly in the trash. Very slick.

The reason for a one star deduction is quite simply for the lack of variety in coffee selections and the higher price of the pods compared to k-cups. I expected to see the dual pod flavor options with the Vertuo like with the Dolce Gusto pods - one coffee and one milk pod for certain combinations. Nonetheless, I really like this coffee maker and I will continue to use it.

reviews.title: Good looking!  Quick!  Coffee not hot enough for me.
reviews.text:
My biggest complaint about this is that "the water does not get hot enough". I like my drinks to be as hot as they can be, and I can't get this hotter without microwaving my coffee.

What is nice about this is that it is petite, looks colorful, and is well-built. The latest technology I have experienced with coffeemakers is one that automatically dumps the used "capsules". The capsule is the name of the pod that holds your expresso/coffee. And, I like that you can adjust the plate for the size of the drink. However, the small capsule lets out 1.35 oz of espresso. That is a small amount.

This is quick! Operates in quick time, quick touch, starts quick, works easily, and open it up, and ZIP..... it dumps the used carousel in the container on the right. This sounds a little loud, but one can get used to it. With the size, you should be able to put it comfortably under any cupboard on the countertop if that is all the place you have to put it.

So, all in all, I like this, because I think 15 second is tooooo quick to heat the drink. I like my coffee hotter. But, what a treat that the company supplies a sample box of coffee and espresso sizes. I have tried a few flavors. and this gives you ideas on what flavors to order next.

reviews.title: great coffee/expresso maker
reviews.text: So in the interest of weaning myself off of the Starbucks habit, I got this. It doesn't take up much counter space (which is nice), while it doesn't take the traditional K-cup it does have a bit of a selection, and it's easy to use (take out of the box, plug in, make sure the light is steady, clean the water container and fill, and there you go - I didn't need to clear the air lines at all). reviews.title: We love this coffee maker
reviews.text: It is a very basic, no frills sort of k-cup coffee maker, but for us that is actually exactly why we like it so much.  No reservoir or filters to fuss with, just fill the cup you're using with the amount of water you want, pour it into the back tank, pop a k-cup into the holder, press the entire cover down until it locks, and push the button.  In a couple minutes you've got a perfect cup of coffee.  A very hot, perfect cup of coffee.  You can actually hear this thing heating up the water and see the steam coming off the finished cup.  This little machine does one thing and does it perfectly.  It looks nice, too, and doesn't take up a lot of space.  In direct comparison to a comparable Keurig I would definitely go with this machine instead.  The price was in the same range for both and this one just looks, feels, and performs at a much higher level.

reviews.text:
I wish I read the description better before buying this.
This is a single serve K-Cup maker, but it's ALSO a single cup tank capacity coffee maker. This means that you need to refill the tank for every single cup you brew.
For a family of 4 it's too much wait because the coffee maker needs to heat the water every single time instead of being able to brew several back-to-back cups.
I recommend this ONLY if you are making just 1 (or max 2) cups at a time.

The button to open the cover is very poorly made as it's hard to lift and the lid gets fairly stuck as well...

The flavor is good and the unit is very compact, so it's great for specially small kitchens.

Overall 3/5.

reviews.title: 2 reviews in 1: Copper mugs keeps it hot hot, stainless steel keeps it warm & drinkable
reviews.text:
This is a review for the 14 ounce COPPER mug, and the 12 ounce STAINLESS STEEL mug.

Update Aug 2022: My review below (from 2019) is for the short squat silver mugs that I bought back in 2019. I recently purchased the COPPER colored geometric shape cup as part of a "copper" themed 7th wedding anniversary gift for my husband (Aug 2022). SO I will add out experience with that mug here. Also grabbed some [[ASIN:B01L9YVAAY Copper Moon Keurig coffee]] to go with it.

He texted me from work, "copper mug works, but omg it holds heat. Have to transfer to my ceramic mug to drink in a timely fashion. Who the hell wants scalding hot coffee an hour later?" I respond, "most people"

Gave me a chuckle, and thought I would add it to the review. He likes his coffee drinkable. Not necessarily cool, but not hot hot. The silver mugs (below) will lose heat, but it holds coffee very well, and keeps it warm enough to be drinkable. This copper mug will keep it hot hot for some time. Perfect for those that want hot coffee for as long as possible. Seems very secure, air tight. THE GRIP IS GREAT. Cool looking too. LOVE the look of the copper color. Has a.. copper appearance. Not a flat color. Fits under my Keurig if I pop out the tray. Smaller mug reviewed below fits underneath without any adjustment.

------------------------------------------------------------------
Original review for STAINLESS STEEL 12 ounce mug written Feb 2019: I bought two, one each for my husband and me. It is a 12oz travel mug with a silicone band for grip and protection from the hot. The base has piece of grip material, that will help it from sliding and also from making loud bang noise when being set down (say on a table during a conference call where all sounds are amplified). The lid is sturdy and quite secure. I filled the cup, closed it up, then tipped it upside down. No leaks! The contents does not stay super hot for very long. I didn't time it, but it kept the contents warm enough and long enough to have a nice cup of coffee/tea. Because it is 12oz, you have to figure out which brewing level will work best for you. Just black? make 12oz if your Keurig has that configuration (or two 6oz). Like cream and sugar? Go for 10oz so you have room to add the other items. I like that it isn't a huge cup, though I also like using the larger ones. It is just a handy little size, and feels good in the hand. I haven't had it long enough to determine it's durability. I suspect that the bottom grip material could pull off if the cup sits in water. It isn't made for long term heat retention, so consider that as well. Overall good cup, just not a perfect cup.

Update Feb 2020: Came back nearly a year later to say that our two Keurig travel mugs are still holding up, and that they are now my preferred travel mug. I am currently getting rid of any other travel mug and buying two more of these.
